name: Tales of Lanchuan
title: Tales of Lanchuan
description: Half of Lanchuan lives on the water. Escort boats read the ferrymen’s lights, mountain temples teach their own forms, and city tea stalls remember old debts. When the rivers rise, even a disputed crossing must make room for travelers.

lanchuan-l01.name: Lankou City
lanchuan-l01.content:
* **Region**: Lankou (The head port city on the north bank of the Lanchuan River, where it enters the sea).
* **First Impressions**: The masts of thousands of seagoing vessels stand dense as a withered forest. When the bronze bell of the Qingfu Bank chimes, storefronts along the entire length of the avenue take down their door-shutters. Old garrison soldiers sit chewing flatbread beneath the gate archway, cradling their spears, beside a crooked wooden placard that reads: "Inspection of Travel Permits."
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Fan Shouzhuo (Chief of the Qingfu Guild), Su Xiaoman (Apprentice bookkeeper), Guan Shanhai (Head of the Zhenhai Martial Arts Hall and external disciple of the Mount Tai Sect), along with a vast multitude of porters and traveling merchants.
* **Livelihood**: Maritime loading and unloading, salt and iron brokerages, martial arts apprenticeships, transit exchange and money remittance.
* **Keep in Mind**: On the first day of every month, the martial arts hall sets up an arena by the docks for public sparring; in the Qingfu Guild's back courtyard, clerks are often seen counting government silver ingots stamped with secret marks.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day east to Tidewatch Ferry; one day north along the coast to Green Salt Shoals; four days upriver by boat to reach Qinghe City in Sihuai.

## Contacts and everyday life

This is Lankou’s main city, not the same street as every coastal location. The exchange counter handles drafts, Zhenhai handles lessons and freight yards can discuss loading. Each has its own responsible people. Fan’s private accounts and the school’s rear courtyard do not open merely because someone strolls through town.

Arrivals from Tide Ferry and Qingyan bring talk of departures and salt prices. Distinguish eyewitness boat crews from repeated shop talk and tavern boasting. In a dispute, seeking a shopkeeper as witness, consulting a trade contact or leaving are all plausible. A gate inspection does not enrol anyone in a school.

lanchuan-l02.name: Tidewatch Ferry
lanchuan-l02.content:
* **Region**: Lankou (An ancient north-south crossing point at the mouth of the great river).
* **First Impressions**: Two stone tide-marking steles, blackened from long immersion in seawater, stand upon the muddy flats. Two flat-bottomed wooden boats are hitched to mooring posts. In front of the old ferryman's hut hangs an oilcloth straw cape, while a yellow dog curls up dozing near the gangplank.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Song Laolu (The old ferryman) and the ferry families.
* **Livelihood**: Plying ferry oars, selling rough tea, and combing the mudflats for seafood during low tide.
* **Keep in Mind**: From the rafters of Song Laolu's hut hangs an old oilpaper umbrella with broken ribs, untouched for nineteen years; the wind lanterns warding the waves at the ferry never go dark at night.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day north back to Lankou City; half a day south to Egret Fishing Village; one day southeast to climb Tidewatch Cliff.

## Contacts and everyday life

The ferry is a land-and-water junction in Lankou. Its tea shelter offers rest; departures depend on a boatman’s current consent. Song’s hut is a home, not a public store of clues. A journey to Lankou City, Egret Village or Tidewatch Cliff starts by asking whether to take shore or water, not by treating a heard name as arrival.

Tide, light and load can change a skipper’s decision. Waiting or seeking another destination is ordinary. Catches, lamps and boatmen’s arguments reveal local conditions, while old cases and injuries still require actual witnesses. Delivering a letter is one possible concern. Refusing, delaying or travelling elsewhere leaves meals to cook and boats to mend.

lanchuan-l03.name: Egret Fishing Village
lanchuan-l03.content:
* **Region**: Lankou (A natural fishing village on the southern shore of the estuary).
* **First Impressions**: Pale gray fishing nets cover the mudflats, where flocks of white egrets wade in the mire. Several dozen low-thatched huts sit backed against the hills facing the sea. Under an old locust tree at the entrance to the village, several sun-baked, shirtless men mend boats and patch nets.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Lan Ali (The fisherwoman) and dozens of fishing households, young and old.
* **Livelihood**: Casting nets at sea, drying fish, and delivering fresh seafood to the grand restaurants of Lankou City.
* **Keep in Mind**: The fishing village and Green Salt Shoals are separated only by a line of wooden stakes; illicit salt smugglers often attempt to pull up the stakes to expand their evaporation ponds, leading to frequent skirmishes.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day north to Tidewatch Ferry; half a day south to climb Tidewatch Cliff.

lanchuan-l04.name: Green Salt Shoals
lanchuan-l04.content:
* **Region**: Lankou (Official and illicit salt pans along the coast north of Lankou City).
* **First Impressions**: An endless expanse of grayish-white salt terraces, brine glistening under the autumn sun. Mountainous mounds of coarse hemp sacks are piled before the salt sheds, while several salt guards bearing short blades patrol back and forth along the wicker fences.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Gu Huaiyuan (Chief of the Salt Gang), and over sixty salt guards and laborers.
* **Livelihood**: Sun-drying salt, washing salt, and nocturnal salt smuggling.
* **Keep in Mind**: Gu Huaiyuan feeds sixty mouths under his command and enforces strict discipline; whenever a salt transport arrives at the shore, the bookkeepers must check the secret seals three times before clearing it.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day south down the coast to Lankou City; directly facing Egret Fishing Village across the mudflats to the southwest.

lanchuan-l05.name: Tidewatch Cliff
lanchuan-l05.content:
* **Region**: Lankou (A perilous crag at the southern tip of the estuary).
* **First Impressions**: Sheer rocks rise like chiseled walls. Perched atop the crag, a two-story timber lodge creaks perpetually in the sea breeze—this is the Tidewatch Inn. The stone terrace behind the cliff is named Dongyue Platform, an outpost retreat established here by the Mount Tai Sect to observe the dawn.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Xu Zhu (Keeper of the Tidewatch Inn and a former operative of the Rain Listening Pavilion) and garrison disciples sent down by the Mount Tai Sect.
* **Livelihood**: Lodging traveling merchants, observing the tides, and forwarding confidential waterborne correspondence.
* **Keep in Mind**: At dawn, disciples of the Mount Tai Sect can often be seen practicing swordsmanship facing the sun on the Dongyue Platform; Xu Zhu roasts exceptionally spicy fish and keeps his mouth as tight as forged iron.
* **Connections & Travel**: Descend the northern cliff path for half a day to Egret Fishing Village; the mountain road is treacherous and easily turns slick in rainy weather.

lanchuan-l06.name: Hedu Town
lanchuan-l06.content:
* **Region**: Qingping Lake (A commercial hub on the northern shore of the lake).
* **First Impressions**: Bluestone streets are grooved deep by heavy freight carts, with shops on either side hung with bronze bells and colorful banners. At the entrance to the town stands a sprawling estate behind high blue-brick walls, flying an escort banner adorned with a golden wild goose on a cyan ground—the headquarters of the Goose-Flight Escort Agency.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Huo Qianli (Chief of the Goose-Flight Escort Agency), Yan Xiaowu (Caravan outrider), and various traveling merchants and middlemen.
* **Livelihood**: Armed escorts and property guarding, land and water cargo transit, warehouse storage.
* **Keep in Mind**: The sound of escort masters drilling with sabers in the back courtyard roars like thunder at dawn; rumors have recently spread that a crate of tribute porcelain escorted by the agency was chipped along the Ten-Mile Embankment, stirring rampant gossip among traders.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day by water to the Duckweed Anchorage water redoubt; one day to Mist-and-Wave Manor; two and a half days north by overland road directly to the foot of Mount Shaoshi.

## Contacts and everyday life

Hedu is a freight stopping town on the northern lake shore; the escort headquarters is only one part. Inns house travellers, warehouses store cargo and the duty escort receives enquiries. Entering for a meal grants no right to take weapons, inspect books or join a convoy.

Boats from Fuping bring lake news while travellers from Shaoshi report northern roads; their accounts may disagree. Comparing a client’s claimed loss with what a worker saw of a damaged crate can precede any decision to intervene. Lake and northern routes retain their travel and access conditions despite an escort banner. Loading, cart repairs, practice and rest belong here as much as old clues.

lanchuan-l07.name: Duckweed Anchorage
lanchuan-l07.content:
* **Region**: Qingping Lake (The main water redoubt hidden among southwestern waterways and bays).
* **First Impressions**: Over a hundred large wooden vessels are moored bow to stern, forming a floating market street interconnected by wooden planks, while sunken stakes bristle through the reed beds. High above the bow of the flag-ship flutters the faded Surge-and-Wave banner.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Ge Changgao (Old master of the Surge-and-Wave Boat Gang), his daughter Ge Qing, and several hundred boatmen.
* **Livelihood**: Waterborne escort transports, lake ferry crossings, fishery and aquatic trade.
* **Keep in Mind**: The veteran boatmen are in fierce dispute over "instituting new rules to distribute shares to smaller boat operators"; many crewmen wear water-diving daggers fitted with barb hooks tucked into their waistbands.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day by boat to Hedu Town; one day heading west upriver to enter the Mount Taihe waterways.

lanchuan-l08.name: Water-Chestnut Village and Foothills of Wild Goose Peak
lanchuan-l08.brief_description: Water-Chestnut Village and Foothills of Wild Goose Peak.
lanchuan-l08.content:
* **Region**: Qingping Lake (Water country along the lake's southern shore, reaching directly to the base of Mount Heng).
* **First Impressions**: Small bridges cross flowing waters through bamboo groves, where water-chestnut gathering girls hum soft tunes from their floating wooden tubs. Behind the village looms Wild Goose Peak, home to the Mount Heng Sect's mountain gate, its ancient trail shrouded in mist.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Disciples under Liu Zhengfeng of the Mount Heng Sect (Xiang Danian, Mi Weiyi), Aunt Lian (The chestnut gatherer), and a despondent elder of Mount Heng who often plays the flute at the village entrance.
* **Livelihood**: Harvesting water chestnuts, weaving bamboo wicker, cultivating lotus roots for medicine, and supplying fresh mountain produce to the Mount Heng Sect.
* **Keep in Mind**: Liu Zhengfeng's residence is currently decked with lanterns and festive draperies, preparing for his Golden Basin Hand-Washing Ceremony following the Double Ninth Festival; mournful and sorrowful huqin melodies can often be heard from the tea stall at the village entrance.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day's ascent south to Mount Heng's Zhurong Peak; one day's boat crossing to Mist-and-Wave Manor.

lanchuan-l09.name: Three Willows Inn
lanchuan-l09.content:
* **Region**: Qingping Lake (A strategic bottleneck along the ancient eastern embankment leading out of the region).
* **First Impressions**: Three ancient willow trees shade half the courtyard, and the inn's banner simply bears a single large character: "Rest." The hearth fire never dies throughout the year, and a great cauldron constantly simmers with hot ginger broth and assorted cured meats.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Auntie Zhong (The innkeeper), long-term guests running tabs, and couriers changing mounts.
* **Livelihood**: Lodging and meals, providing fresh mules and horses, safekeeping baggage for regular patrons.
* **Keep in Mind**: A guest room in the back courtyard has been kept locked for years, cleaned daily by Auntie Zhong herself; though she greets everyone with a beaming smile, she flicks her abacus beads with razor-sharp precision.
* **Connections & Travel**: Two days east along the Ten-Mile Embankment to Sangma Town in Sihuai; one day west by overland road into Hedu Town.

lanchuan-l10.name: Mist-and-Wave Manor
lanchuan-l10.content:
* **Region**: Qingping Lake (An ancient manor secluded on an isolated island in the lake's center).
* **First Impressions**: A grand mansion of blue brick and white plaster stands hidden deep within dense lake mists, its stone steps accommodating only a single dugout canoe at a time. Before the gate stands a spirit screen with faint calligraphy: "Mist and waves run chill; guests are bid return."
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Manor Master Rong Jiugao (A supreme swordsman of the elder generation) and two mute old servants.
* **Livelihood**: Self-sustaining through private fields and ponds inside the manor; closed to outside guests for twenty years.
* **Keep in Mind**: The corner window shutters of the manor's library tower are all nailed shut; on windless late nights, a remarkably plaintive zither melody often drifts across the water's surface.
* **Connections & Travel**: Surrounded on all sides by water, inaccessible except by boat; row one day to reach either Hedu Town or Water-Chestnut Village.

lanchuan-l11.name: Qinghe City
lanchuan-l11.content:
* **Region**: Sihuai (The premier metropolis of the Jianghuai region, a major transit port by water and land).
* **First Impressions**: Ten-zhang-high gray city walls enclose a bustling, prosperous market. To the west of the city, a three-story timber tower with flying eaves rises majestically, hung with a dark lacquered plaque that reads "Rain Listening Pavilion"; ragged beggars with hemp sacks tied at their waists are visible everywhere throughout the streets.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Yan Shier (Master of the Rain Listening Pavilion), Qiao Buduan (The storyteller), eight-pouch duty elders of the Beggars' Sect, and prominent merchants of various trades.
* **Livelihood**: Grand canal transport tax offices, selling scripts and calligraphy, teahouses and wine shops, intelligence broking.
* **Keep in Mind**: The ground floor of the Rain Listening Pavilion serves coarse tea and hosts storytelling, the second floor handles drafts and remittances, while the third cannot be entered without an iron medallion; every afternoon when Qiao Buduan tells tales, the entire hall falls dead silent.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day east to Caokou Market; half a day north to Old Locust Anchorage; one day west to Sangma Town; two days drifting downstream to Lankou City.

lanchuan-l12.name: Caokou Market
lanchuan-l12.content:
* **Region**: Sihuai (A canal anchorage market east of Qinghe City).
* **First Impressions**: Hemp sacks are piled like mountains while thousands of bare-chested porters dash across gangplanks in rhythm with their work chants. The air is thick with the scent of aged rice, salted fish, and sour sweat, punctuated by the sharp clack of bamboo tallies thrown down by the foremen.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Pu Xiaoqi (A low-ranking disciple of the Beggars' Sect), freight foremen, dock laborers, and street vendors.
* **Livelihood**: Grand Canal cargo loading and unloading, heavy porterage, selling flatbreads and coarse tea.
* **Keep in Mind**: In a corner of the market, an old beggar always rests with closed eyes, holding a chipped ceramic bowl; whether passersby give much or little, he merely nods slightly, never uttering a word of entreaty.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day west back to Qinghe City; one and a half days downriver by boat directly to the estuary at Lankou.

lanchuan-l13.name: Old Locust Anchorage
lanchuan-l13.content:
* **Region**: Sihuai (A sprawling compound in the wilderness north of Qinghe City).
* **First Impressions**: Beneath an ancient locust tree broad enough to require four people to encircle it sits a weathered compound of dilapidated gray tiles. Over the gate hangs a giant, broken stoneware alms bowl suspended by hemp ropes; inside the courtyard, three massive iron caldrons boil porridge, sending up rolling clouds of cooking smoke.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Lu Youjiao (Chief of the Beggars' Sect, or elder statesmen of the prior generation), Chen Youliang (Duty elder), Niu Bushi (Conservative elder), and hundreds of sect members.
* **Livelihood**: Distributing grain provisions to branch sects across the realm, collecting union guild dues along the canal, providing relief to the aged and weak.
* **Keep in Mind**: Deep palm prints are indented upon a martial practice boulder in the courtyard corner, breaking off abruptly at the twelfth strike; disciples of the Clean Clothes faction and the Dirty Clothes faction sit on separate sides of the dining hall.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day south to the bustling streets of Qinghe City; the ancient post road to Mount Shaoshi connects to the northwest.

lanchuan-l14.name: Ten-Mile Embankment
lanchuan-l14.content:
* **Region**: Sihuai (An ancient official flood-control levee leading toward Qingping Lake).
* **First Impressions**: Old willows cast shade along both sides of the elevated rammed-earth embankment, where aquatic grasses grow wild. Every three miles stands a thatched tea stall providing travelers with a place to rest and take shelter from the rain.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Levee maintenance workers, tea stall couples, and long-distance pack caravans.
* **Livelihood**: Brewing tea and selling water, maintaining the levee banks, guiding passing mule carts.
* **Keep in Mind**: During rains, the soil of the embankment turns loose and hides numerous pitfalls; a weathered, fractured stone stele retains only half its inscription: "...undisturbed by surging waves."
* **Connections & Travel**: One day east into Sangma Town; two days west to Three Willows Inn at Qingping Lake.

lanchuan-l15.name: Sangma Town
lanchuan-l15.content:
* **Region**: Sihuai (A prosperous sericulture town bordering land and water routes).
* **First Impressions**: Every household in the town raises silkworms and weaves silk fabrics, and clean white raw silk floats in the water channels. In the center of town sits a grand wooden opera stage, where visiting troupes frequently reside, keeping the air filled with singing and the music of strings and pipes throughout the day.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Bai Henian (Troupe master of the Spring Pear Troupe), Hongxiao (Martial female lead), Jiang Qinghe (Female physician at Qinghe Herbal Hall), and wealthy weaving households.
* **Livelihood**: Mulberry cultivation and silk reeling, touring opera performances, trade in wound-healing medicinal herbs.
* **Keep in Mind**: One side of the opera stage's support pillar is riddled with woodworm, troubling the troupe master over repair costs; Jiang Qinghe possesses superb medical skills, and poor locals are always queued outside her door seeking remedies.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day east into Qinghe City; one day west to the Ten-Mile Embankment; when winter arrives, the troupe follows the river to take shelter from the cold at the foot of the Western Peak.

lanchuan-l16.name: Shaolin Monastery
lanchuan-l16.content:
* **Region**: Shaoshi (An ancient, premier Buddhist monastery beneath Shaoyang Peak on Mount Shaoshi).
* **First Impressions**: The thousand-year-old mountain gate stands solemn and majestic, its vermilion gates bearing an ancient imperial plaque. Beyond lies the Mahavira Hall, shrouded in incense smoke as bells and drums sound in unison. Before the Guest Reception Hall, a spring-fed stone basin provides visiting pilgrims with refreshing water.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Abbot Xuanci, Xuanji (Head of the Discipline Hall), Xuannan of the Bodhidharma Hall, Xuzhu (The earnest and awkward young reception monk), and hundreds of martial monks in dark robes.
* **Livelihood**: Collecting monastic land rents, soliciting incense offerings, dispensing herbal medicine from the Buddhist infirmary.
* **Keep in Mind**: Access to the Sutra Pavilion is strictly guarded, with senior monks of the Bodhidharma Hall rotating watches day and night; young Xuzhu bustles about the Guest Reception Hall serving vegetarian noodles, hurriedly joining his palms in greeting whenever he meets someone.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day down from the mountain gate to Front Temple Street; half a day through the rear mountain path to the Pagoda Forest; branch north to the Thread-of-Sky Cliffway.

lanchuan-l17.name: Front Temple Street
lanchuan-l17.content:
* **Region**: Shaoshi (The commercial thoroughfare nestled at the foot of Shaolin's mountain gate).
* **First Impressions**: A steep bluestone street climbing the slope, flanked entirely by incense shops, scripture-copying workshops, vegetarian noodle stalls, and mule inns. Pale smoke and white mist drift about, amid an unceasing din of vendors' hawking cries.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: The old broth noodle vendor (An elderly townsman secretly watched by the Mount Song Sect), Ji Wenmo (Proprietor of the scripture-copying workshop), innkeepers, and pilgrims from all quarters seeking Buddhist wisdom.
* **Livelihood**: Incense and candle sales, transcription of Buddhist sutras, vegetarian dining and lodging, mule and porterage services.
* **Keep in Mind**: External disciples of the Mount Song Sect, bearing Five Mountains command banners at their waists, frequently wander the street corners under the pretext of hunting wanted outlaws, secretly probing the identities of travelers entering and leaving Shaolin.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day's ascent to the Shaolin gate; one and a half days south to Wheat Yellow Village; one day north to the precipices of Thread of Sky.

lanchuan-l18.name: Mount Song Sect's Taishi Compound
lanchuan-l18.content:
* **Region**: Shaoshi (The main headquarters on Mount Taishi, separated from Mount Shaoshi by a single peak).
* **First Impressions**: The stone stairs are exceptionally steep. Built of rugged black stone, the mountain gate flies hunting banners whipped by the wind, embroidered with a giant broadsword of gold and five-colored talismans. The halls are austere and imposing, exuding a stern, martial aura.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Zuo Lengchan (Leader of the Mount Song Sect, who rarely descends the peak), Ding Mian (First Grand Guardian), Fei Bin (Second Grand Guardian), and over a hundred sect swordsmen.
* **Livelihood**: Levying protection tributes from manors across the Central Plains, taking cuts from escort agencies, welcoming pledged disciples.
* **Keep in Mind**: Disciples form ranks to practice swordplay before the mountain gate, their sweeping strikes impenetrable to wind and rain; emissaries from various sects carrying secret missives frequently arrive seeking audience with Alliance Leader Zuo amid a tense atmosphere.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day down Shengguan Peak connects to the Mount Shaoshi post road; turn east for two days to reach the Huai River basin.

lanchuan-l19.name: Pagoda Forest
lanchuan-l19.content:
* **Region**: Shaoshi (Deep in the pine woods behind the main resident halls of Shaolin).
* **First Impressions**: Hundreds of spirit pagodas of gray stone and carved brick honor eminent monks, carpeted in thick moss while wind soughs through the pines like weeping. Deepest within stands a fractured, waist-high stele devoid of inscriptions, resting lonely and hidden in the overgrown weeds.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: The broom-wielding old monk guarding the pagodas (With deep, reserved inner light) and young novices who routinely bring vegetarian meals.
* **Livelihood**: Sweeping the pagoda grounds, tending the tomb pagodas of past patriarchs.
* **Keep in Mind**: The outer stone pagodas are open to pilgrims, but loitering near the deep stele is strictly forbidden; every dawn, the old monk sweeps the ground, leaving the blue bricks spotless wherever his broom passes.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day's walk along the flagged path from the rear courtyard of Shaolin; no path leads to the outer mountain.

lanchuan-l20.name: Wheat Yellow Village and Thread of Sky
lanchuan-l20.brief_description: Wheat Yellow Village and Thread of Sky.
lanchuan-l20.content:
* **Region**: Shaoshi (Adjoining the temple's wheat fields to the south, and guarding the narrow gorge of Thread of Sky to the north).
* **First Impressions**: Golden waves of wheat stretch across the fields at the edge of the village, where boundary stones mark "Permanent Domain of Shaolin"; passing the village to the north, one encounters the Thread-of-Sky plank road cleaved like two knife-cut cliffs overlooking a bottomless gorge.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: The old tenant village elder, Chang Xiaoqiu (The accounting woman), and plank road repair craftsmen.
* **Livelihood**: Tilling tenant fields, collecting agricultural taxes, maintaining the cliffways.
* **Keep in Mind**: Discrepancies between this year's monastic field ledgers and the villagers' private plots have caused disputes, but the locals dare not speak up; iron chains hang along the Thread-of-Sky plank road, where weathered boards sway suspended in the wind.
* **Connections & Travel**: Two days south to Hedu Town at Qingping Lake; two days north across Thread of Sky to Linghe Ferry on Frost Ridge.

lanchuan-l21.name: Yingxian Town
lanchuan-l21.content:
* **Region**: Mount Taihe (A market town at the foot of Mount Wudang).
* **First Impressions**: Bluestone streets are lined on both sides with tea shops, large copper kettles steaming with white vapor and filling the air with rich tea aromas. The weathered "Immortal Welcoming Archway" at the town entrance has been eroded by time; beneath it, lay disciples of Wudang maintain stalls year-round to offer tea.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Tu Dahu (Head merchant of the tea exchange, well-versed in Daoist medicine), tea farmers, visiting mountain pilgrims, and external affairs deacons of Wudang.
* **Livelihood**: Tea wholesale and trade, monastery procurement, hosting visiting believers from all directions.
* **Keep in Mind**: Conceited wandering blades frequently brag at the town entrance about ascending the mountain to test their skills against Wudang masters, only to be turned away embarrassed by the smooth, gentle persuasion of the tea shop hands.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day up to Cloud-and-Mist Tea Slopes; one day's climb up the Hundred-Step Stairs directly to Purple Cloud Temple; three days drifting downriver by boat to Qingping Lake.

## Contacts and everyday life

Yingxian lies below Taihe Mountain. Tea shops, lodging and supply merchants are reachable before ascending; being below Wudang is not being inside Zixiao Temple. Visitors may ask prices or directions, and registered students may work in town or visit acquaintances.

The tea slopes require care for cultivated paths; the Hundred-Step ascent depends on health and weather. Separate tea-shop rumours of a challenge from confirmed temple arrangements. Tu Dahu has his own trade and observations, not the abbot’s voice. Food, supplies and harvest continue whether someone climbs or stays. Taking vows does not determine the legitimacy of the story.

lanchuan-l22.name: Cloud-and-Mist Tea Slopes
lanchuan-l22.content:
* **Region**: Mount Taihe (A thousand acres of sun-drenched terraced tea fields halfway up the mountain).
* **First Impressions**: Terraced tea rows undulate along the mountain terrain, with mists swirling around the ankles. At the crest stands an elegant Daoist lodge where Wudang elders often come to boil tea and contemplate the Dao.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Qu Aqiao (The stubborn tea-plucking girl), over a dozen elderly tea-farming households, and young acolytes tending the herb garden.
* **Livelihood**: Harvesting selected tribute mist-tea, cultivating Daoist herbs.
* **Keep in Mind**: At the summit grows the thousand-year-old "Mother Tree," wide enough to require two people to encircle; this year its shoots have turned withered and yellow, leading farmers to suspect unusual water seepage beneath the earth veins.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day down the mountain back to Yingxian Town; half a day upward connects to the Hundred-Step Stairs.

## Contacts and everyday life

The slope is cultivated land. The mother tree, channels and picking paths have custodians; it is not an unowned herb field. Qu Aqiao may show the section she tends, while picking, digging and testing treatments require the growers’ consent.

Buyer reports from town, herbal advice from Jiang Qinghe and a woodcutter’s experience are distinct sources. One rotten root proves neither poisoning nor a cured hillside. Help may be as small as clearing a channel or lifting a basket. If the tree cannot be treated, visitors may still shop, ask directions or leave while growers discuss how to survive the season.

lanchuan-l23.name: Hundred-Step Stairs and Lonely Pine Pavilion
lanchuan-l23.brief_description: Hundred-Step Stairs and Lonely Pine Pavilion.
lanchuan-l23.content:
* **Region**: Mount Taihe (Steep stone steps suspended along the precipice leading to Purple Cloud Temple).
* **First Impressions**: Three thousand stone steps climb straight into the clouds, flanked by ancient pines as rugged as iron. A four-cornered ancient pavilion juts out halfway up the mountain above a fathomless abyss, with a lone pine standing proud on the cliff edge beside it.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Resting pilgrims, pack porters, and a disheveled Daoist who has recently taken to sitting alone, drinking while embracing his blade (Shen Guhe, a former disciple of Wudang).
* **Livelihood**: Carrying grain and transporting masonry, selling straw sandals and mountain water.
* **Keep in Mind**: Shen Guhe sits alone each day in the Lonely Pine Pavilion, stroking an iron sword tightly bound in white cloth; without speaking, he watches passing Wudang disciples with cold, silent eyes.
* **Connections & Travel**: More than half a day down to Yingxian Town at the foot; half a day's climb to reach the Purple Cloud Temple esplanade.

lanchuan-l24.name: Purple Cloud Temple
lanchuan-l24.content:
* **Region**: Mount Taihe (The principal temple of the Great Mountain, situated beneath Zhanqi Peak on Mount Taihe).
* **First Impressions**: Red walls and turquoise tiles nestle amid verdant ancient cypresses; the Sanqing Hall stands grand and solemn, its golden roof glinting amidst the clouds. On the wide white stone terrace before the hall, a dozen young Daoists breathe in unison with the wind, their palm techniques fluid and circular, moving slow as if caressing water.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: Song Yuanqiao (Eldest of the Seven Heroes of Wudang, managing general affairs), Yu Lianzhou, Mo Shenggu, Song Qingshu (Senior disciple of the third generation), Yunshu (A young Daoist nun), and over a hundred Daoist clergy (Patriarch Zhang Sanfeng is in seclusion in the grottoes of the rear mountain).
* **Livelihood**: Daoist incense rituals, leasing temple farmland, practicing charity and dispensing medicine.
* **Keep in Mind**: The temple emphasizes quietude and detached tranquility; anyone seeking tutelage or sparring must first stay three days in the lower lodge to temper their restlessness; behind the main hall lies an Ink-Washing Pool, its water tinged with faint black.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day descending along the Hundred-Step Stairs; half a day through the dense rear mountain woods leads into the secluded Heart-Cleansing Ravine.

## Contacts and everyday life

Within Taihe Mountain, Zixiao’s reception hall, guest rooms, teaching courts and rear retreats are separate spaces. The Hundred-Step path approaches from below; Xixin Ravine has another mountain trail. Moving between them still requires actual travel and permission.

Yunshu may receive students and relay requests. Teachers have lessons and retreats; naming one does not make them appear. A visitor may ask a limited question outside, wait for class, help with supplies or descend. Discussing a technique is not learning it, acquaintance is not permission to take vows or accept a challenge for someone else, and rumours need not force every student into one duel.

lanchuan-l25.name: Heart-Cleansing Ravine
lanchuan-l25.content:
* **Region**: Mount Taihe (A perilous, rarely trodden gorge deep behind Purple Cloud Temple).
* **First Impressions**: A secluded, chilly mountain ravine where stream boulders are coated in green moss. Two humble thatched huts are built against the cliffside, dried firewood and strings of red peppers hanging under the eaves; the wattle gate rests ajar, shaded by ancient pines behind the house.
* **Notable Inhabitants**: An old woodsman calling himself "Old Woodcutter Tao" (Qi Wujiu, harboring a supreme secret regarding the Beggars' Sect) and mountain villagers who occasionally cross the peaks to fetch fire embers.
* **Livelihood**: Felling timber for fuel, gathering wild ginseng to barter for oil and salt.
* **Keep in Mind**: The old woodcutter's hair is white as frost and he appears decrepit, yet he walks swiftly over jagged rocks bearing two hundred catties of wet pine logs; a chipped, coarse ceramic alms bowl sits year-round in the corner of his hut.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day's trek over the mountain to return to Purple Cloud Temple; one day descending along the wild stream trail winds out toward the tea slopes.

lanchuan-l26.name: Jade Maiden Peak of Mount Hua
lanchuan-l26.brief_description: Jade Maiden Peak of Mount Hua.
lanchuan-l26.content:
* **Region**: Cangwu Ridge (the absolute summit of the Western Sacred Mount, ancestral seat of the Mount Hua Sect).
* **First Impressions**: Wind howls through ancient pines atop the sheer precipice, where antique halls nestle along perilous crags. The plaque over the main hall reads "Hall of Rectitude." Beneath it, disciples in white robes wield green-steel blades, their sword stances light, nimble, and soaring. Beside the peak towers the impassable Ear-Rubbing Cliff, while the lonely, precarious Cliff of Contemplation looms starkly behind.
* **Inhabitants**: Sect Leader Yue Buqun and his wife Ning Zhongze; second disciple Lao Denuo, sixth disciple Lu Dayou, and Yue Lingshan; Linghu Chong is serving his confinement on the Cliff of Contemplation.
* **Livelihood**: Estate land rents, stipends and tributes from Guanzhong merchants.
* **Points of Interest**: The solitary Cliff of Contemplation stands isolated with its mountain path sealed off; only Lu Dayou climbs up daily to deliver meals. Yue Buqun frequently reads scrolls in his study, sitting on the merger letters sent by the Mount Song Sect without replying.
* **Connections & Travel**: Descending Ear-Rubbing Cliff and passing Thousand-Foot Precipice leads to Iron Cable Bridge Post within one day; a secret path through the back mountains allows exploration of Huichun Valley.

lanchuan-l27.name: Iron Cable Bridge Post
lanchuan-l27.content:
* **Region**: Cangwu Ridge (the throat of Mount Hua, an ancient iron-chained bridge wedged between two cliffs).
* **First Impressions**: Several dark-red iron chains as thick as a child's arm span an abyss tens of thousands of feet deep, their wooden planks swaying violently in the gale. At the bridgehead stands a small posthouse built solidly of green stone, its hearth kept piping hot day and night.
* **Inhabitants**: Station master Ke Qiaotou (formerly a veteran swordsman of Mount Hua's outer sect), along with several hands wrapped in aged sheepskins.
* **Livelihood**: Guarding the bridge, inspecting passing merchants, and serving hot wine and dry rations.
* **Points of Interest**: Crossers must hook their hands onto iron rings and keep their footwork steady; timid travelers often collapse here in sheer terror. Ke Qiaotou has a single, eagle-sharp eye and can gauge the depth of a traveler's internal energy merely from the rhythm of their footsteps across the bridge.
* **Connections & Travel**: Heading east down the mountain reaches Jinxi Town in one day; heading west up the mountain reaches the front gate of the Mount Hua Sect in one day; heading northwest reaches the Yanbei border pass in six days.

lanchuan-l28.name: Jinxi Town
lanchuan-l28.content:
* **Region**: Cangwu Ridge (a bustling medicinal market nestled in a sheltered valley at the southern foot of Mount Hua).
* **First Impressions**: A small brook winds through the settlement, its flanking streets and lanes packed with stalls of angelica, codonopsis, fritillary, and gentiana macrophylla, filling the air with a bitter medicinal aroma. At the end of the street stands an opera stage, where troupes from the Lichun Troupe rest their horses.
* **Inhabitants**: Guildmaster Luo Banxia of the Medicine Guild, traveling herbal traders, resident apothecaries, and veteran artists remaining from the Lichun Troupe.
* **Livelihood**: Wholesale herb transactions across Guanzhong, Sichuan, and Shaanxi; opening scales for herbal markets; running taverns and inns.
* **Points of Interest**: Every mid-month during the herb market opening, merchants and mountain foragers argue until red-faced over price undercutting. Prescriptions from Huichun Hall are treated as hard currency throughout town.
* **Connections & Travel**: Reaches Huichun Valley in half a day; climbs to Iron Cable Bridge Post in one day; crosses the mountains eastward to reach Mount Taihe in five days.

lanchuan-l29.name: Huichun Valley
lanchuan-l29.content:
* **Region**: Cangwu Ridge (a warm, moist medicinal valley embraced by towering peaks).
* **First Impressions**: A wooden arch at the valley mouth bears the four characters "Practicing Medicine to Deliver the World." Inside, terraced fields clinging to the slopes are planted entirely with exotic herbs. Wisps of medicinal smoke drift from several green-bamboo apothecary cottages, accompanied by the ceaseless thudding of pestles.
* **Inhabitants**: Hall Master Du Ruo of Huichun Hall (a generational physician), physicians Cheng Zhiwei and Bai Qian (who is obsessed with toxicology), and the young herb-gathering girl A'Ling.
* **Livelihood**: Treating wounds, concocting secret life-saving powders, and supplying top-grade trauma medicines to major sects.
* **Points of Interest**: Heavily locked secret chambers in the inner hall preserve ancestral poison compendiums and medical case files. Recently, wounded disciples from both the Mount Hua and Mount Song sects have covertly sought treatment here; Du Ruo strictly enforces an iron rule of "all blades sheathed upon entering the valley."
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day's walk out of the valley leads to Jinxi Town; heading north along the hidden crags of the back mountain for one day reaches Mist-Locked Ravine.

lanchuan-l30.name: Mist-Locked Ravine
lanchuan-l30.content:
* **Region**: Cangwu Ridge (a perilous, desolate ravine sealed off year-round by poisonous miasma).
* **First Impressions**: The entrance is enshrouded in vast, pale poison fog; inhaling even a trace leaves a sickly sweet taste in the throat. Deep in the ravine lies an obscure medicine hut built of black bamboo, surrounded by fences choked with eerie purple-flowered vines.
* **Inhabitants**: The eccentric former medical master Mo Wensheng and several vicious hounds.
* **Livelihood**: Refining poisons and testing medicines deep in the mountains; dissolving rare, deadly gu parasites for notorious outlaws.
* **Points of Interest**: Mo Wensheng's fingernails are tainted faint purple, and his temper is bizarre and erratic. The ravine is strewn with bone-rotting herbs; no one should set foot inside without ingesting Huichun Valley's Miasma-Warding Pills.
* **Connections & Travel**: A day's trek south leads back to Huichun Valley, though the trail is treacherous and a single misstep means plummeting into the abyss.

lanchuan-l31.name: Wild Goose Fall Pass
lanchuan-l31.content:
* **Region**: Yanbei (a formidable bottleneck fortress connecting the central plains to the great desert).
* **First Impressions**: A weather-beaten, ochre stone gate tower hangs an imperial iron tablet reading "Pacify the North" beneath its grand battle flag. The arched gate tunnel is jammed with mule and horse caravans awaiting travel pass inspections, while all inns inside the pass fly large banners reading "Detain Guests" and "Facing the Wind."
* **Inhabitants**: Pass Commandant Sun, Manager Zhongxia of the Yanbei Branch of the Yanxing Escort Agency, merchants from beyond the frontier, and rotating garrison border troops.
* **Livelihood**: Inspecting travel passes, running horse stables and inns, levying frontier trade taxes, and maintaining escort agency garrisons.
* **Points of Interest**: Commandant Sun inspects seals rather than faces—so long as official passes and paperwork are in order, passage is granted. Recently, small scouting units of Mongol horsemen and scouts from the Black Stone Post outlaws have frequently roamed beyond the pass.
* **Connections & Travel**: An eight-day journey southeast along the imperial road leads straight to Mount Shaoshi in the Central Plains; half a day outside the pass leads to Camel Bell Mart; two days northwest reaches Black Stone Post.

lanchuan-l32.name: Camel Bell Mart
lanchuan-l32.content:
* **Region**: Yanbei (an open oasis bazaar outside the pass).
* **First Impressions**: Over a hundred camels form circular corrals across the sands, the ring of bronze bells carrying for miles. Felt yurts and timber shacks interlock in jagged lines, piled everywhere with Qinghai steeds, sheepskin liners, compressed brick tea, and fine steel sabers.
* **Inhabitants**: Horse-trader proprietress Ma Sanbao (harboring secret secular ties to the Mount Heng Sect), Hui merchants from the Western Regions, and interpreters.
* **Livelihood**: Trading fine horses, renting camels, and reselling pelts and tea bricks.
* **Points of Interest**: Ma Sanbao commands the finest paced horses beyond the northern frontier, but she enforces a strict rule: those who do not understand a horse's temperament cannot lead a single steed away, even for a thousand taels of gold.
* **Connections & Travel**: Half a day southeast leads back to Wild Goose Fall Pass; two days due north leads into the Rocky Crags of Black Stone Post.

lanchuan-l33.name: Black Stone Post and the Rocky Crags
lanchuan-l33.brief_description: Black Stone Post and the Rocky Crags.
lanchuan-l33.content:
* **Region**: Yanbei (a strategic desert gorge and bottleneck beyond the northern pass).
* **First Impressions**: Jagged, pitch-black stones charred like coal stand in eerie thickets; wind howling through the rock crevices sounds like the weeping of ghosts and wailing of spirits. Deep within the stone labyrinth stands a fortified stockade of green stone and rammed earth, bearing a large Black Stone banner outside its gates.
* **Inhabitants**: Overlord of the Rocky Crags Li Changfeng (formerly one of the Seven Companions of Lanchuan, wielding the Cloud-Splitting Spear) and dozens of fierce frontier outlaws.
* **Livelihood**: Operating a post station, levying reasonable road tolls, and providing route-guarding guides for major merchant caravans.
* **Points of Interest**: Li Changfeng takes toll fees strictly within reason and never kills needlessly; he secretly sends half of his silver and grain to Sand Spring Village to build canals and relieve the poor. Every Double Ninth Festival, he closes his gates to drink alone, refusing all guests.
* **Connections & Travel**: Two days south leads back to Wild Goose Fall Pass; one day southwest leads to the Sand Spring Village oasis; a day and a half northwest reaches the abandoned Severed Beacon Tower.

lanchuan-l34.name: Sand Spring Village and Kongtong Terrace
lanchuan-l34.brief_description: Sand Spring Village and Kongtong Terrace.
lanchuan-l34.content:
* **Region**: Yanbei (a red-stone isolated terrace and oasis settlement deep in the desert gravel).
* **First Impressions**: A pool of emerald spring water appears abruptly amid barren sands, surrounded by swaying willows and scattered adobe houses. West of the village rises a reddish-brown, loaf-like cliff terrace resembling an inverted censer—an outer outpost of the Kongtong Sect.
* **Inhabitants**: Old Canal Elder Grandfather Qin (a Kongtong veteran bearing lingering scars from the Seven-Injuries Fist) and dozens of households descended from garrison soldiers.
* **Livelihood**: Channeling spring water for irrigation, cultivating melons and wheat, and providing water and grain to passing travelers.
* **Points of Interest**: An ancient stone trough in the village rations water with immaculate fairness; travelers must leave a single copper coin to draw water. Young and old in the village alike practice horse-stance thrust punches beneath the stone terrace every morning.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day east leads to Black Stone Post; one day north leads to Severed Beacon Tower; traveling west leads toward the grand headquarters of the Kongtong Sect in Pingliang.

lanchuan-l35.name: Nature-Perceiving Peak of Mount Heng
lanchuan-l35.content:
* **Region**: Yanbei (the precarious canyon cliff of Northern Mount Heng).
* **First Impressions**: Dozens of flying pavilions and vermilion halls hang suspended across a hollowed vertical cliff face hundreds of feet high, supported only by standing timber pilings, with plank bridges strung like gossamer. Clouds billow past beneath one's feet, and the crisp chime of Buddhist bells echoes long through the gorge.
* **Inhabitants**: Mount Heng Sect Leader Abbess Dingxian, Abbess Dingyi, junior sister Yilin, and dozens of dark-robed Buddhist nuns.
* **Livelihood**: Begging alms, distributing congee, maintaining ancient mountain paths, and dispensing medicine to poor frontier women and children.
* **Points of Interest**: Abbess Dingyi is fiery-tempered, yet the disciples within the convent are gentle and compassionate. Yilin recites scriptures before the Buddha daily, her expression often tinged with lingering longing. Letters demanding the Five Mountains Merger have been delivered up Nature-Perceiving Peak multiple times.
* **Connections & Travel**: Descending the suspended plank paths leads to the northern foot of Wild Goose Fall Pass in one day; winding around mountain trails westward enters the northern frontier grasslands.

lanchuan-l36.name: Cold Pine Keep
lanchuan-l36.content:
* **Region**: Frost Ridge (a timber-and-stone fortress at the foot of snowy peaks).
* **First Impressions**: Thick fortress walls assembled from giant stones are hung with icicles, and chimneys along the street billow straight plumes of gray smoke. Furrier shops, smithies, and distilleries interlock; hunters carrying longbows stride swiftly across the snow in deerskin snow boots.
* **Inhabitants**: Chief Lei Baishan of the Cold Mountain Hunting Guild, female snow-route guide Lan Xue, fiery tavern proprietress Xin Erniang, along with tanners and smiths.
* **Livelihood**: Big-game hunting in snowfields, trading mink and fox furs, distilling strong liquor, and serving as mountain guides.
* **Points of Interest**: Outside Xin Erniang's distillery hangs a wooden sign: "Dust off your snow before stepping inside; if you don't, this lady will dust it off for you." Lei Baishan enforces an unbending rule never to hunt pregnant beasts.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day east leads to Red Furnace Manor; a day and a half southwest leads to Ice River Ferry; heading north along the Ancient Falling Snow Path reaches the snow peaks of Mount Kunlun in two days.

lanchuan-l37.name: Red Furnace Manor
lanchuan-l37.content:
* **Region**: Frost Ridge (an ancient forging compound built against a sheltered rock wall).
* **First Impressions**: Three blast furnaces thirty feet tall vomit scarlet flames day and night, their deafening hammer strokes audible miles away. At the entrance stands a wrought-iron stele half the height of a man, carved with a single character: "Forge."
* **Inhabitants**: Manor Master Yan Hanlu (the premier master smith of the north), his granddaughter Yan Ji, and dozens of bare-chested brawny smiths.
* **Livelihood**: Mining and smelting iron, forging divine blades and swords for various sects, and supplying armor-piercing arrowheads to the hunting guild.
* **Points of Interest**: The "Furnace Vault" in the back courtyard remains locked year-round; rumors say it holds "Half-Inch Frost," an unfinished masterwork sword blank forged nineteen years ago. Old Manor Master Yan's temper is fiery; anyone deemed unworthy to wield a blade cannot buy a scrap of iron from him, even for ten thousand taels of gold.
* **Connections & Travel**: One day west leads to Cold Pine Keep; winding south along mountain trails reaches Ice River Ferry in three days.

lanchuan-l38.name: Ice River Ferry
lanchuan-l38.content:
* **Region**: Frost Ridge (a major glacier ferry crossing at the boundary between Shaoshi and Frost Ridge).
* **First Impressions**: The wide river churns violently here, its flanking cliffs draped in frozen waterfalls. Beside the crossing stands a row of ancient pines, fronting a wooden lodge marked with a black lacquer board: "Punt flat-bottom boats in summer; march over yard-thick ice in winter."
* **Inhabitants**: Veteran ferryman Feng Binghe (trained in Kunlun breath-guiding techniques) and two or three ice-clearing laborers.
* **Livelihood**: Punting ferry boats, chipping channels through ice, and steering north-south wayfarers clear of hidden ruts in the frozen river.
* **Points of Interest**: Every morning before dawn, Feng Binghe taps the ice with an iron chisel, cocking his ear to listen to the resonance of ice veins. Outsiders think he is daydreaming, but he is actually practicing the Daoist art of "Listening to the Ice."
* **Connections & Travel**: Traveling south for a day and a half through Thread of Sky leads directly onto Shaolin Temple Front Street; heading north for a day and a half reaches Cold Pine Keep.

lanchuan-l39.name: Kunlun Three Sages Hall
lanchuan-l39.content:
* **Region**: Frost Ridge (the zenith of the Ancient Falling Snow Path, atop the Kunlun snowline).
* **First Impressions**: Nestled in a snow-carpeted mountain col, magnificent Daoist palaces rise against the snowy peaks. The glazed tile roofs of the Three Purities Hall reflect a crystalline blue beneath the sun. Before the entrance stand two colossal banners of the Supreme Ultimate, radiating chilling sword intent.
* **Inhabitants**: Kunlun Sect Leader He Taichong ("Mr. Iron Zither"), his wife Ban Shuxian, and disciples Xihuazi and Wei Siniang.
* **Livelihood**: Harvesting Kunlun jade, sharing profits from cold iron veins, and receiving tributes from Western Region merchant caravans.
* **Points of Interest**: He Taichong appears dignified and poised, yet lives in utter dread of his wife; Ban Shuxian is harsh and unyielding. The Liangyi Swordplay created by the couple dominates the northwest, and their gates are guarded so strictly that outsiders are rarely allowed a glimpse.
* **Connections & Travel**: Following the ancient path down the snow mountains reaches Cold Pine Keep in two days; scaling the western snow slopes leads straight into the Western Region wastelands and the outer perimeters of Bright Peak of the Ming Cult.

lanchuan-l40.name: Snow-Listening Thatched Cottage
lanchuan-l40.content:
* **Region**: Frost Ridge (an extremely secluded snow cliff flanked by ancient pines at the end of the Ancient Falling Snow Path).
* **First Impressions**: Three rustic log cabins stand backed against a snowy crag, their roofs burdened under three feet of snow while a wisp of faint smoke rises straight into the sky. Before the yard sits a small well, the wooden bucket on its rim wiped spotless without a speck of grease or grime.
* **Inhabitants**: A gaunt, white-haired traveler styling himself "Master Liu" (Liu Chenzhou, former leader of the Seven Companions of Lanchuan) and an aged hunting hound guarding the gate.
* **Livelihood**: Chopping firewood, growing greens, and occasionally repairing broken bows for hunters.
* **Points of Interest**: Master Liu wipes every item in the cottage clean every morning; on the table rests a pair of chipped green jade paperweights. He speaks sparingly, his brow weighed down by an unyielding guilt spanning nineteen years.
* **Connections & Travel**: About a day and a half of snowy march from Cold Pine Keep; when heavy snow blocks the mountains, only the most seasoned hunters can locate the trail by following tree notches.

lanchuan-o01.name: Shaolin Sect
lanchuan-o01.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Permanent Abode on Mount Shaoshi in the Central Plains; Temple Front Street serves as the foot-of-the-mountain checkpoint.
* **Sect Heritage**: All martial arts under heaven stem from Shaolin. Majestic and solemn, it houses hundreds of monks under strict monastic disciplines, seldom meddling in petty jianghu feuds.
* **True Livelihood**: Hundreds of qing of monastic farmland across Mount Shaoshi and Maihuang Village, incense offerings from widespread devotees, woodblock printing of Buddhist sutras, and compounding miraculous trauma medicines.
* **Foundational Arts**: *Yijin Jing* (the supreme scripture of the Sutra Library), Great Vajra Finger, Arhat Fist, and Reed Crossing the River lightness skill.
* **Internal Currents**: Abbot Xuanci enjoys high virtue and prestige, yet deep sorrow often locks his brow; Head Monk Xuanji of the Discipline Hall strictly guards sect secrets to prevent the Sutra Library from leaking; Xuan'nan of the Bodhidharma Hall worries the Mount Song Sect will use the Five Mountains Alliance to erode Shaolin's prestige; guest-reception monk Xuzhu greets visitors on Temple Front Street, merely hoping to avoid the discipline ruler during daily morning and evening classes.
* **Mundane Intersections**: Novices dining at the Old Broth Noodle Stall on Temple Front Street or copying sutras in the workshop for lodging can forge ties with Shaolin's periphery; the Guest Reception Hall dispenses tea rather than martial arts—those seeking authentic Shaolin teachings must first pass tests of character.

lanchuan-o02.name: Wudang Sect
lanchuan-o02.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Zixiao Temple on Mount Taihe in Hubei; Welcome Immortal Town sits at the mountain foot.
* **Sect Heritage**: The pinnacle of orthodox internal martial arts, standing equal to Shaolin. Following the Dao of nature, it values cultivating qi, keeping the center, and overcoming movement through tranquility.
* **True Livelihood**: Shares in the Welcome Immortal Town tea guild, land rent from Misty Tea Slope, temple medicinal herb gardens, and Daoist incense offerings from across the realm.
* **Foundational Arts**: Taiji Fist, Taiji Sword, Pure Yang Boundless Skill, Liangyi Qi-Nurturing Formula, and Cloud Ladder Step.
* **Internal Currents**: Grandmaster Zhang Sanfeng remains in secluded cultivation researching supreme Daoist principles; Great Hero Song Yuanqiao manages internal and external affairs with broad benevolence; Second Hero Yu Lianzhou possesses eagle-sharp eyes that see through worldly deceit; young chief disciple Song Qingshu is talented and handsome, yet overly proud; Shen Guhe, who stormed off down the mountain in anger ten years ago, vows to return this Double Ninth Festival to challenge the sect, asking "can Taiji draw blood?"
* **Mundane Intersections**: Sipping rough tea from Tu Dahu's bowls at the Welcome Immortal Town tea stalls, or running into Mo Shenggu descending the Hundred Steps Stair on sect duties; those with Daoist destiny can borrow handwritten fragments of the *Liangyi Qi-Nurturing Formula*.

## Contacts and everyday life

Wudang teaches disciplined breathing, restraint and charitable medicine. Zixiao Temple handles internal affairs; Yingxian Town and the misty tea slopes supply tea, herbs and provisions. Their residents are not sect property. Yu Lianzhou can advise registered students, Yunshu oversees daily lessons, and Qu Aqiao cares about the tea harvest.

Rumours of Songshan pressing other schools into union make armed visitors harder to receive. Relations with tea merchants and travelling healers rest on earned trust. Registration explains a visitor’s background; it grants neither access to the rear mountain nor permission to borrow scriptures or accept a duel for a teacher. Joining requires personal willingness and the school’s consent, with lessons and restraint as continuing duties. Making a living below the mountain is equally legitimate. Returning borrowed goods earns particular people’s trust; trading on the temple’s name damages it.

lanchuan-o03.name: Ming Cult
lanchuan-o03.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Bright Peak west of the far-western Frost Ridge; maintains secret warehouses and branch altars across Yanbei and the Si-Huai waterways.
* **Sect Heritage**: Unruly and unyielding, walking the line between good and evil. Defying imperial tyranny, it rallies righteous warriors across the realm, its members spread through workshops, grain canals, and desert trade paths.
* **True Livelihood**: Transshipping jade and treasures from the Western Regions, bartering horse herds in the desert, running covert river workshops in Jianghuai, and raising supplies for rebel armies across worldly branches.
* **Foundational Arts**: Great Shift of the Universe, Nine Yang Divine Art (Cult Leader Zhang Wuji), and Strange Sacred Flame Token movement techniques.
* **Internal Currents**: Cult Leader Zhang Wuji is benevolent and kind, striving to dissolve a century of blood feuds with the Six Major Sects; Princess Shaomin, Zhao Min, unmatched in resourcefulness, stays by his side, leveraging princely mansion power and martial undercover networks to back each other; yet the Five Element Banners and non-clan wanderers still harbor deep grudges over Shaolin and Mount Hua's past siege.
* **Mundane Intersections**: In the Yanbei desert or Caokou Mart docks, players often encounter Five Element Banner brethren flying merchant guild banners; so long as one does not stir up trouble, Ming Cult members hold oaths of brotherhood and righteousness in the highest regard.

lanchuan-o04.name: Beggars' Sect
lanchuan-o04.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Old Locust Dock north of Qinghe City in Si-Huai (Headquarters); branch posts sit along every major river dock.
* **Sect Heritage**: The realm's largest guild, numbering hundreds of thousands, with the widest social ties and sharpest eyes and ears. Divided into the Clean-Robed and Dirty-Robed factions.
* **True Livelihood**: Loading, unloading, and managing canal freights in Lianghuai; port porter fee shares; doorstep begging; providing overland caravan escorts.
* **Foundational Arts**: Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms (the first twelve palms survive; the latter six are lost), Dog-Beating Staff Technique, and Hundred-Knot Divine Skill.
* **Internal Currents**: Sect Leader Lu Youjiao is upright and straightforward, sticking to the code that beggars never forget their roots; Eight-Pouch Elder Chen Youliang is shrewd and scheming, consorting with officials and gentry to seize canal transport authority; the secret of former missing sect leader Qi Wujiu's severed palm lies buried in Heart-Cleansing Ravine on Mount Taihe, a subject sect elders fiercely avoid.
* **Mundane Intersections**: Hauling a load of rice at Caokou Mart or sharing half a cold steamed bun in a dilapidated shrine can win the acquaintance of two-pouch or three-pouch disciples; those versed in beggars' cant travel unhindered across the waterways and roads of Lianghuai.

lanchuan-o05.name: Mount Song Sect
lanchuan-o05.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Sheng Guan Peak Headquarters on Mount Taishi, across the ridge from Shaoshi.
* **Sect Heritage**: Seat of the Grand Alliance Leader of the Five Mountains. Its swordplay is solemn and monumental, its style domineering and fierce, placing supreme weight on status and intimidating dominance.
* **True Livelihood**: Profits from mines, iron foundries, and salt pans across the Central Plains; tributes extracted from travelers along imperial trade roads; taking in disciples from prominent clans.
* **Foundational Arts**: Five Mountains Swordplay: Mount Song Forms (solemn, majestic, and disciplined), Great Songyang Divine Palm, and Frigid Ice True Qi internal art.
* **Internal Currents**: Alliance Leader Zuo Lengchan aims to annex the other four sects, suppress Shaolin and Wudang, and unify the martial world; First Guardian Ding Mian and Second Guardian Fei Bin roam the lands suppressing dissidents; sect disciples maintain checkpoints at the foot of Mount Shaoshi, bringing their covert feud with Shaolin Temple into the open.
* **Mundane Intersections**: At the tea shelters on Temple Front Street, one often spots arrogant sword-bearing Mount Song warriors flashing Five Mountains command flags to blockade roads and seize travelers at will, leaving ordinary folk furious but silent.

lanchuan-o06.name: Mount Hua Sect
lanchuan-o06.content:
* **Seat & Portals**: Hall of Rectitude on Jade Maiden Peak along the sheer cliffs of Cangwu Ridge's Western Mount.
* **Sect Heritage**: Orthodox line of the Western Mount, famed for swordplay that is light, nimble, perilous, and unorthodox. Severely weakened since the past rift between the Sword and Qi factions, its numbers are few, but its reputation remains upright.
* **True Livelihood**: Protection tributes from Guanzhong trade routes, timber and medicinal yields from the mountain base, and alliances with esteemed scholar clans.
* **Foundational Arts**: *Violet Mist Manual* (the foremost among Mount Hua's nine arts), Five Mountains Swordplay: Mount Hua Forms, and Sunrise Single-Character Sword.
* **Internal Currents**: Yue Buqun strains tirelessly to uphold his spotless name as the "Gentleman Sword," feeling outmatched by Mount Song's pressure; Ning Zhongze remains fiercely principled; eldest disciple Linghu Chong, punished for his unruly love of wine and mingling with the demonic cult, is confined to the Cliff of Contemplation for a year; second disciple Lao Denuo appears steady and discreet, yet harbors treacherous motives.
* **Mundane Intersections**: In the wine taverns of Jinxi Town and Iron Cable Bridge Post below, one frequently overhears tales of Linghu Chong running up tabs, or bumps into Lu Dayou purchasing trauma ointments in apothecaries.

lanchuan-o07.name: Mount Heng Sect
lanchuan-o07.content:
* **Region**: Zhurong Hall on Returning Goose Peak, south shore of Lake Qingping.
* **Sect Heritage**: Distinguished lineage of the Southern Mount. Its swordplay is endlessly erratic, weaving musical rhythms into sword forms, characterized by an untrammeled and artistic demeanor.
* **True Livelihood**: Waterway escorts along the Xiao and Xiang rivers, yields from lake paddies, and the immense private wealth of Liu Zhengfeng.
* **Foundational Arts**: Five Mountains Swordplay: Mount Heng Forms, Hundred-Transformation Thousand-Illusion Cloud and Mist Sword of Mount Heng, and Whirling Wind Falling Goose Sword.
* **Internal Currents**: Second-in-command Liu Zhengfeng commands immense personal wealth and is mobilizing the sect to prepare his Golden Basin Hand-Washing Ceremony on the Double Ninth Festival, vowing to cut ties with all martial feuds; Sect Leader Master Mo Da drifts through streets with a huqin fiddle, drawing mournful melodies while watching the upcoming ceremony with cold detachment, suspecting catastrophe looms ahead.
* **Mundane Intersections**: At tea shelters in Lingge Village or the Three Willows Inn, one may unexpectedly run into a gaunt, elderly man in a blue cotton gown, cradling a worn huqin and playing *Night Rain on the Rivers Xiao and Xiang*.

lanchuan-o08.name: Hengshan Sect
lanchuan-o08.content:
* **Region**: Hanging Temple on Jianxing Peak, north of Luoyan Pass, Yanbei.
* **Sect Heritage**: A Buddhist nun branch advocating compassion, forbearance, and detachment from worldly contention. Its swordsmanship excels in dense, close defense, concealing sharp counter-thrusts within steadfast parries.
* **Livelihood**: Alms from frontier devotees, distributing medicinal tea, and taking in women orphaned or widowed by warfare.
* **Supreme Arts**: Five Sacred Mountains Swordplay: Hengshan Stance (Cotton Needle Stance, airtight and seamless), Ten Thousand Flowers Swordplay.
* **Internal Currents**: Sect Leader Abbess Dingxian is benevolent and perceptive; having long seen through Zuo Lengchan's ambitions of sect annexation, she adamantly refuses to submit. Abbess Dingyi is fierce and fiercely protective, quick to draw her sword and berate foes. Junior Sister Yilin is pure and innocent, spending her days in fervent prayer and apprehension over conflicts down the mountain.
* **Worldly Interactions**: Outside the gates of Luoyan Pass and before Camel Bell Market, young Hengshan nuns often descend to distribute medicine to passing refugees. Gentle in manner, they are held in immense esteem by escort guards and camel caravans traversing the northern wastes.

lanchuan-o09.name: Mount Tai Sect
lanchuan-o09.content:
* **Region**: Dongyue Terrace behind Wangchao Cliff at Lankou; grand headquarters at Jade Emperor Peak, Mount Tai, Shandong.
* **Sect Heritage**: A major Daoist lineage of the Eastern Peak, its swordsmanship is austere, archaic, and immense, crashing down with the grandeur of Mount Tai pressing overhead.
* **Livelihood**: Toll cuts from river-sea salt transport, Daoist pilgrim taxes from Sun-viewing Peak, and revenue splits from coastal lay fist-fighting gyms.
* **Supreme Arts**: Five Sacred Mountains Swordplay: Mount Tai Stance, Mount Tai's Eighteen Turns, Daizong Ruohe (secret ancient calculation technique).
* **Internal Currents**: Sect Leader Daoist Tianmen is unyielding and upright, unable to tolerate even a speck of dust in his eyes, bearing deep hatred for wicked and unorthodox ways. However, senior elders like Yujizi and Yuyinzi have put profit before righteousness, secretly swayed by the Songshan Sect's hefty bribes, leaving the sect on the brink of schism.
* **Worldly Interactions**: Around the dueling platforms of Lankou City and along Wangchao Cliff, Mount Tai Daoists frequently step in to suppress frictions involving illicit salt and sea pirates, acting in a rigid, cold, and uncompromising manner.

lanchuan-o10.name: Emei Sect
lanchuan-o10.content:
* **Region**: Cloud-Crest Nunnery (Emei Golden Summit Traveling Palace) deep within Baicao Col, Cangwu Ridge.
* **Sect Heritage**: A Buddhist-Daoist lineage founded by Grandmaster Guo Xiang, composed primarily of women. Bound by chillingly strict sect laws, they take subjugating demons and subduing wickedness as their sworn duty, striking with swift, resolute severity.
* **Livelihood**: Tax silver from the Sichuan-Shaanxi Tea Horse and medicinal herb trade, and tenant rents from pious benefactors across various regions.
* **Supreme Arts**: Emei Nine Yang Skill, Wind-Swirling Willow Swordplay, Nine Intercepting Hands; the Sect Leader wields the divine weapon, the Heavenly Sword.
* **Internal Currents**: Sect Leader Abbess Miejue possesses an unyielding, ruthless temperament, having sworn to annihilate the Demon Cult while enforcing terrifying discipline upon her disciples. Her favored disciple, Zhou Zhiruo, is outwardly gentle yet inwardly gifted, quietly enduring the jealousy of her martial siblings alongside the crushing weight of her master's expectations. Her senior sister, Ding Minjun, is caustic and petty, constantly hunting for faults to stir up trouble.
* **Worldly Interactions**: In the medicinal markets of Jinxi Town, one occasionally encounters veiled, sword-bearing Emei swordswomen procuring rare, prepared medicinal ingredients; common roughnecks give them a wide berth, daring not step out of line.

lanchuan-o11.name: Kunlun Sect
lanchuan-o11.content:
* **Region**: Three Sages Hall of Kunlun, situated along the Snowfall Ancient Road in the Far North Frost Ridges.
* **Sect Heritage**: An ancient sword sect dwelling far out in the Western Regions, holding sole dominion over the perilous snowy ridges. Its disciples bear a cold, haughty demeanor and excel in combined strike formations.
* **Livelihood**: Wholesale and retail of Kunlun mutton-fat white jade, transit taxes along Western trade routes, and the mining of cold iron from the snow-capped peaks.
* **Supreme Arts**: Orthodox Dual Liang Swordplay (conforming to the permutations of Yin and Yang), Snowfall Flying Sand Palm.
* **Internal Currents**: Mr. Iron Zither He Taichong maintains a facade of dignity; though his swordsmanship is exquisite, his heart is petty and narrow. Grand Sect Leader Ban Shuxian is wild-tempered, headstrong, and tyrannical. Disciple Xi Huazi is vain and eager for glory, burning with desire to establish Kunlun's prestige within the mountain passes.
* **Worldly Interactions**: Disciples of Kunlun frequently appear around the blacksmith shops and pelt trade houses of Frostpine Keep. Arrogant in speech, they hold most Central Plains sects in utter disdain.

lanchuan-o12.name: Kongtong Sect
lanchuan-o12.content:
* **Region**: Kongtong Terrace Grand Headquarters, on the western cliffs of Sandspring Village, Yanbei.
* **Sect Heritage**: A mighty fist-fighting sect of the Northwest emphasizing heavy, unyielding power, rough and ferocious in conduct, guarding the strategic throat of Longdong.
* **Livelihood**: Escorting northern frontier merchant caravans, leading camel-train convoys through mountain passes, and taking dividends from horse markets.
* **Supreme Arts**: Seven Injuries Fist (one training inflicts seven injuries, an internal force capable of shattering mountains and crumbling boulders), Flying Phoenix Hand, Divine Fist Sect Softening Force.
* **Internal Currents**: The Five Elders of Kongtong—Guan Neng, Zong Weixia, Tang Wenliang, and their peers—are well advanced in years. Due to long years of arduous Seven Injuries Fist cultivation, their internal organs suffer backlash from hidden wounds, turning their tempers increasingly short and fiery; they are frantic to seize rare healing elixirs across the Jianghu.
* **Worldly Interactions**: Near the Water-Dividing Well in Sandspring Village, third-generation Kongtong disciples regularly oversee irrigation. Though their fists are as hard as stone, they still harbor a deep, protective bond of shared incense with the villagers of their ancestral soil.

lanchuan-p01.name: Song Laolu
lanchuan-p01.brief_description: The old ferryman who has rowed flatboats at Tidewatch Ferry for decades. Everyone who meets him must respectfully address him as Old Song. Beneath the eaves of his thatched hut hangs an old umbrella with broken ribs, which he never allows anyone to touch.
lanchuan-p01.content:
* **Location / Identity**: Tidewatch Ferry · Old Ferryman; former veteran of the Surge Boat Gang, retired from the Jianghu for thirty years.
* **Appearance**: Back arched like a bow, left ear missing a corner; perpetually keeps a sparkless copper pipe hanging from the corner of his mouth, his hands covered in thick calluses.
* **First Impression**: The old ferryman who has rowed flatboats at Tidewatch Ferry for decades. Everyone who meets him must respectfully address him as Old Song. Beneath the eaves of his thatched hut hangs an old umbrella with broken ribs, which he never allows anyone to touch.
* **Manner of Speech**: Slow and deep, never straying three sentences from the nature of water. "When a swell hits you head-on, if you fight it, the hull splits; if you bow your head and go with it, it carries you right over."
* **Goals & Daily Life**: Tending the ferry crossing and the night-time wave-warning lanterns; checking the water at dawn, mending nets in the afternoon, lighting the lanterns at dusk.
* **Network**: Once steered the same boat and shared close ties with Ge Changgao, the old helm master of the Surge Boat Gang; often looks after Lan Ali of Egret Fishing Village; once took in the player ("Visitor at the Ferry").
* **[Author Reference]**: The old umbrella under the eaves was left behind nineteen years ago by his daughter, Song Qing, when she left home. Back then, objecting to her father's involvement in the illicit salt disputes, Song Qing stormed off to Qinghe City to become an embroiderer. Riddled with shame, she still dares not return home to this day (triggers Affair A01).

## Contacts and everyday life

He knows local tides, older boat households and events he witnessed, not every port’s secret accounts. Visitors can ask fares, discuss water conditions or sit outside while he repairs an oar. He still eats, rests and watches the weather; he does not wait all day to explain a mystery.

His old friendship with Ge Changgao explains guild history but cannot promise the present pilots’ boats. The umbrella and old grievances are matters he guards. Seeing the object reveals only an old object; whether he speaks depends on his willingness and the conversation. He wants to keep the ferry working and must consider who may eventually take the boat. The player may help, hire another boat or leave old matters alone.

lanchuan-p02.name: Fan Shouzhuo
lanchuan-p02.brief_description: The chief manager overseeing the largest bank at the great river's estuary. His pet phrase is, "Allow this old man to calculate once more." Amid the dense shops of Lankou City, Chief Fan is the only one who can lend out a hundred taels of silver solely on the credit of a person's face.
lanchuan-p02.content:
* **Location / Identity**: Lankou City · Chief Manager of the Qingfu Association.
* **Appearance**: Round-faced like a wealthy squire, clad in a dark-patterned sapphire satin robe, his right hand idly rolling three refined brass abacus beads all day long.
* **First Impression**: The chief manager overseeing the largest bank at the great river's estuary. His pet phrase is, "Allow this old man to calculate once more." Amid the dense shops of Lankou City, Chief Fan is the only one who can lend out a hundred taels of silver solely on the credit of a person's face.
* **Manner of Speech**: Measured and deliberate, every word laced with monetary figures. "Silver does not lie, but men do. Only when the ledger is balanced can the heart find peace."
* **Goals & Daily Life**: Maintaining the remittance trade routes stretching from Jianghuai to the northern frontier; auditing master ledgers at dawn, sipping supreme Longjing tea in the afternoon, inventorying the vaults at dusk.
* **Network**: Master of his apprentice Su Xiaoman; shares an unresolved fifteen-year-old bad debt with Gu Huaiyuan of Green Salt Beach; finances and hires disciples from Zhenhai Martial Arts School to guard the silver vaults.
* **[Author Reference]**: In the major embezzlement scandal at Green Salt Beach fifteen years ago, Fan Shouzhuo secretly tore out a crucial ledger page recording deposited silver to protect the Qingfu Association's reputation. This framed Gu Huaiyuan for absconding with vast sums of money (triggers Affairs A02, A03, and Formidable Foe B1).

lanchuan-p03.name: Su Xiaoman
lanchuan-p03.brief_description: The youngest and most agile clerk in the Qingfu Bank. Her fingers work the abacus faster than ordinary men can speak. Rumor has it that when provoked, she can fling abacus beads like iron pellets straight at an opponent's throat.
lanchuan-p03.content:
* **Location / Identity**: Lankou City · Female Bookkeeping Apprentice of the Qingfu Association.
* **Appearance**: Sports an exceedingly crisp single ponytail, dark arm-guards on her wrists, and thin calluses on all ten fingertips from flicking abacus beads. A heavy ebony-and-brass abacus is tucked diagonally at her waist.
* **First Impression**: The youngest and most agile clerk in the Qingfu Bank. Her fingers work the abacus faster than ordinary men can speak. Rumor has it that when provoked, she can fling abacus beads like iron pellets straight at an opponent's throat.
* **Manner of Speech**: Crisp, sharp, and haggling over every copper. "This favor has been overdue for three days. At two percent interest, that comes to four coppers. Settle now, or put it on your tab?"
* **Goals & Daily Life**: Opening up the silver exchange route from Lankou to Yanbei in the northern frontier; balancing accounts by day, practicing close-quarters abacus grappling in the rear courtyard by night.
* **Network**: Highly accomplished pupil under Fan Shouzhuo; secretly exchanges confidential letters with Zhong Xia, manager of the Wild Goose Escort Bureau at Luoyan Pass; shares a sisterly bond with Ge Qing of the Surge Boat Gang.

## Contacts and everyday life

She trusts drafts she has checked, familiar correspondents and routes she has actually travelled. Being an apprentice does not reveal the old books Fan keeps locked away. Asked about Yanbei, she raises practical questions about payment and guarantors rather than waiting for a stranger to declare a trade route complete.

Ge Qing is a friend to consult about transport, not a servant on call. During bookkeeping Su asks visitors to wait; during practice she does not want to be treated as a free clerk. She hopes to test a dependable new route without losing her teacher’s trust. Small transfers and verification may precede expansion, or risk may delay it. She remembers particular help without turning every friendship into interest or automatically following a traveller.

lanchuan-p04.name: Guan Shanhai
lanchuan-p04.brief_description: A famed martial arts master along the coast. He accepts apprentices without regard for pedigree or bone structure, testing first whether one can haul two buckets of seawater across half a li of mudflat in a single breath.
lanchuan-p04.content:
* **Location / Identity**: Lankou City · Master of Zhenhai Martial Arts School; former outer-sect lay disciple of the Mount Tai Sect.
* **Appearance**: Red-complexioned, built like a bear with tiger-broad shoulders; his right ear was torn by fist wind in an arena duel years ago, crumpled like a cauliflower; his booming voice strikes like a bronze bell.
* **First Impression**: A famed martial arts master along the coast. He accepts apprentices without regard for pedigree or bone structure, testing first whether one can haul two buckets of seawater across half a li of mudflat in a single breath.
* **Manner of Speech**: Gruff, outspoken, and fiercely bound to rules. "Fists are thrown to stop villains from overturning your cooking pot, not to go around smashing someone else's rice bowl."
* **Goals & Daily Life**: Protecting the school's reputation and livelihood along the docks; drilling disciples on wooden stakes at dawn, guiding practical close-quarters grappling in the afternoon.
* **Network**: Acknowledged by Daoist Tianmen as an outer-sect branch of the Mount Tai Sect, though Guan Shanhai steers clear of Mount Tai's internal strife; sworn brother from youth to Gu Huaiyuan of Green Salt Beach; his eldest disciple is Zheng Tieniu.

lanchuan-p05.name: Zheng Tieniu
lanchuan-p05.brief_description: The sturdy pillar among the school's younger generation. He possesses Herculean strength and fights with straightforward honesty in the ring, yet off the platform, he often pays out of his own pocket to treat beaten opponents to bowls of hearty pork noodles.
lanchuan-p05.content:
