But if the Mount Song Sect draws their swords to search the wagons, whoever dares crack open that secret casket will taste the blood on our goose-feather blades."

He slides a heavy brass command tally across the table before you: "A limit of twelve days. You take the secondary wagon and ride with Xiaowu. Do you dare accept?"

Beside him, Yan Xiaowu arches an eyebrow at you and grins, flashing a throat-slitting grimace.

**[Author Reference]**
* **Scene Purpose**: The standardized ritual of taking an escort commission, seamlessly weaving marketplace convoy work into the grand conflict of the Five Mountains Sword Sects' Golden Basin Hand-Washing.
* **Linked Elements**: Task A05 "A Crate of Celadon", Mount Heng Sect Liu Zhengfeng's Hand-Washing case, Mount Song Sect's command banner coercion.
* **Characters Appearing**: Huo Qianli (age 55, Head Escort), Yan Xiaowu (age 21, escort crier/outrider).
* **Tone Benchmark**: Oppressive, austere, the blood-on-the-blade customs of escort agencies.

lanchuan-d11.name: Xin's Tavern on a Snowy Night at Cold Pine Fort
lanchuan-d11.brief_description: Xin's Tavern on a Snowy Night at Cold Pine Fort.
lanchuan-d11.content:
**[Player Visible]**
Outside, the snow has sealed the mountain passes, and a shrieking blizzard howls across the pitch-black night. The snow on the streets of Cold Pine Fort lies a full foot deep. The tavern's thick padded door-curtain is suddenly thrust aside, blowing in a swirl of snowy frost and bone-chilling wind.

Proprietress Xin Erniang holds an old, balding broom, sweeping vigorously toward the door with enough force to knock someone off balance:

"Knock off that snow! Scrape the frozen mud off your boot soles against the stone steps! Enter my establishment bringing snow instead of silver, and you'll get beaten out with a cudgel!"

The interior is intensely warm, a massive iron blast furnace burning scarlet in the center, baking the pine-log walls until they exude a pleasant aroma of toasted rosin. Over a dozen frontier hunters wrapped in thick wolf-pelt cloaks huddle around the fire, drinking amber-colored Xin Family Circulating Liquor by the bowlful, the room thick with the pungent stench of harsh liquor and venison.

Grand Chief Lei Baishan of the Hunting Guild sits right in the center of the hearth, an old leather boot propped on a tree stump, the frostbite scar at the corner of his left eye resembling a purplish-red centipede under the firelight. He pushes a large wooden bowl before you, the liquor boiling hot and searingly pungent:

"Outsider, take a swig to warm your belly. Anyone who can cross Linghe Ferry against this blizzard counts as a tough bastard."

Xin Erniang brings over a large platter of frozen venison sliced paper-thin and slams it onto the table, her voice booming: "Brother Lei, the boys patrolling the front mountain sent word. That Daoist Xihuazi of the Mount Kunlun Sect pitched camp on the snowy slopes with a few young disciples. Too arrogant to take shelter inside the fort, insisting they're hunting some Demonic Cult villain—their faces have turned green from the cold!"

Lei Baishan grunts coldly and drains the fiery liquor in his bowl: "Ignorant, foolish brats. A blizzard on the tundra doesn't give a damn about his purple silk bagua robe. If an avalanche comes down at midnight, no one lift a finger to collect their corpses!"

**[Author Reference]**
* **Scene Purpose**: An indoor sanctuary in an extreme northern glacial fortress, illustrating the harsh glacial environment and the friction between the Mount Kunlun Sect and the hunting guild.
* **Linked Elements**: Task A20 "The Unfinished Sword", Mount Kunlun Sect and Ming Cult friction, Cold Mountain Hunting Guild rules.
* **Characters Appearing**: Xin Erniang (age 45, tavern proprietress), Lei Baishan (age 54, Hunting Guild Grand Chief).
* **Tone Benchmark**: Bold, fiery, rugged, a sharp contrast between extreme northern frost and indoor hearthfire.

lanchuan-d12.name: Gathered by the Hearth Hearing Rumors on a Rainy Night at Iron Chain Bridge Post
lanchuan-d12.brief_description: Gathered by the Hearth Hearing Rumors on a Rainy Night at Iron Chain Bridge Post.
lanchuan-d12.content:
**[Player Visible]**
Mountain gales drive down the clay-and-tile chimney of the tiny post station along the thousand-fathom cliffside, howling continuously. Dense firewood crackles and spits sparks in the hearth. Several peddlers, porters, and retired old soldiers sit cross-legged around the fire with damp felt blankets over their knees, while the crossbeams behind them are hung thick with dried strips of mutton and straw sandals.

"Brothers, have you heard?" A peddler carrying mountain goods tosses a dry pinecone into the fire. "Outside the boulder fields of Black Rock Post, a bloody massacre took place not long ago! Someone rode in alone and clashed with that spear tyrant Li Changfeng amid the dust storm for three whole days and nights!"

"Bullshit!" A horse-trader beside him spits on the floor. "Where did you get three days and nights? It was thirty moves, plain and simple! I saw it with my own eyes—that young swordsman drew his blade, and the sword qi sliced the thirty-foot black stone monument right in half. Li Changfeng dropped his spear on the spot, falling to his knees weeping and begging for mercy!"

"For real? How come I heard an eminent monk from Shaolin's Bodhidharma Hall shattered the tip of Li Changfeng's spear with a demon-subduing pestle?"

Station Master Ke Qiaotou sits in the shadows behind the counter, using a dry rag to slowly wipe a chipped old bronze cup. Listening to them spit and argue, a deep, mocking smile curls the corners of his lips.

He walks over, lifts a boiling-hot iron kettle, refills your cracked porcelain bowl with hot tea, and chuckles under his breath:

"The names are never wrong, and Li Changfeng's Cloud-Cleaving Spear was indeed brandished in the boulder fields. But the cause? Nothing more than an outsider lad delivering a pouch of copper coins for Sandspring Village to repair a canal. Li Changfeng took the coin and treated him to three bowls of fiery grain liquor, that's all. Once a jianghu rumor passes through three gorges, even a dog's bark gets spun into a dragon's roar. Honored guest, in all the stories you hear, which part was actually your doing?"

The firelight flickers. Outside, the long iron chain bridge suspended over the thousand-foot chasm sways violently in the howling storm, groaning like the screech of clashing iron.

**[Author Reference]**
* **Scene Purpose**: A classic demonstration of how martial arts rumors warp and distort, stripping away the artificiality of conventional MMO bulletin-board storytelling.
* **Linked Elements**: Task A19 "The Missing Cargo", Formidable Foe B4 Li Changfeng rumors, vital pass at the foot of Mount Hua.
* **Characters Appearing**: Ke Qiaotou (age 55, Mount Hua Sect elder and Station Master), passing merchants of various sects.
* **Tone Benchmark**: Subtly satirical, deconstructive of marketplace myths, the absurdity and warmth of authentic jianghu lore.

lanchuan-o13.name: Wild Goose Escort Agency
lanchuan-o13.content:
(Headquarters in Hedu Town by Qingping Lake; Branch at Falling Goose Pass in Yanbei)
Head Escort Huo Qianli is as calm as still water, while his young escort crier Yan Xiaowu has a sharp, gossiping tongue. Relying on an ancestral *Route Book* and a goose-feather saber, they have stood firm for twenty years without ever losing a major shipment. Operating combined land and water transport with the Surging Wave Boat Gang, they are currently maneuvering in secret over compensation for a chipped crate of imperial tribute porcelain.

## Contacts and everyday life

Wild Goose Escorts lives on entrusted cargo. Its headquarters is in Hedu Town; lake transfers often involve the boat guild at Fuping Cove, while Zhongxia watches the northern road at Luoyan Pass. The banner matters because people along the road recognise its promises, not because it frightens every armed band. Huo Qianli puts safe delivery first; Yan Xiaowu wants to earn a secure place. They can disagree over taking dangerous work or resting the teams.

A newcomer states their skills, endurance and share of the work before discussing pay. Borrowed weapons and animals must be returned as agreed; affiliation does not open the storeroom. Lake work depends on available boats, northern work on passes and weather. Qingfu remittance reduces carried cash without insuring every loss. Protecting companions and reporting damage honestly earns repeat work; concealed injuries and opened cargo lose trust. Finishing a job leaves room to rest, study or change trades.

lanchuan-o14.name: Rejuvenation Hall
lanchuan-o14.content:
(Rejuvenation Valley in Cangwu Ridge; sales branch in Jinxi Town)
Hall Master Du Ruo established the iron rule of "quench all blades upon entering the valley," earning a reputation across Qinchuan for practicing medicine to heal the world. In the valley, the healer Cheng Zhiwei saves lives with pragmatic care, while Bai Qian secretly studies toxicology, the two locked in overt and covert rivalry. Meanwhile, the outcast Mo Wensheng, the Poison Hand, remains a rotting scar that Rejuvenation Hall has not dared uncover for twenty years.

lanchuan-o15.name: Qingfu Guild
lanchuan-o15.content:
(Headquarters in Lankou City)
The largest official-and-private banking firm and exchange hub at the river estuary. Guildmaster Fan Shouzhuo is a master of the bronze abacus, speaking of nothing without referencing the ledgers. Apprentice Su Xiaoman harbors grand ambitions, determined to expand Qingfu drafts into the northern Yanbei desert, training relentlessly in close-quarters combat using an abacus as a lethal weapon.

## Contacts and everyday life

Qingfu maintains remittance through cash reserves, clerks and correspondents at its Lankou headquarters. Fan Shouzhuo protects the old books; Su Xiaoman wants a route to Yanbei. Boat transport and escort services are necessary partnerships, not servants commanded by a draft. The old Qingyan accounts keep Fan and Gu Huaiyuan distrustful.

Ordinary customers may ask rates, verify drafts and remit money. A familiar guarantor helps checking, not automatic exemption from security or interest. A would-be clerk needs a willing teacher, accurate work and discretion about customers. Learning bookkeeping grants no access to the till. A suspicious mark calls for checking its number and provenance, not accusing the entire association. Reputation follows particular completed transfers, delays and explanations; it is not universal credit at every branch.

lanchuan-o16.name: Rain-Listening Pavilion
lanchuan-o16.content:
(Three-story wooden pavilion with sweeping eaves in Qinghe City, Sihuai)
The preeminent intelligence agency in the realm. Pavilion Master Yan Shier cradles bitter tea, boasting the creed: "Never tell a lie, never tell the whole truth." On the ground floor, storyteller Qiao Buduan spins jianghu gossip into tales to baffle prying ears; the second floor audits accounts, while the hidden chamber on the third floor holds the deepest secrets of every renowned master and sect under heaven.

lanchuan-o17.name: Surging Wave Boat Gang
lanchuan-o17.content:
(Great Water Fortress at Duckweed Dock, Qingping Lake)
The overlords of the eight-hundred-li Qingping Lake. Old Helmsman Ge Changgao, lame in one leg, anchors his boat, while his daughter Ge Qing wields a long pole to champion new rules so that thousands of small fisherfolk can share in the profits of grand canal transport, arguing red-faced with stubborn old boatmen at the bow.

## Contacts and everyday life

The Canglang boat guild makes its living from vessels, skilled pilots and dock transfers at Fuping Cove. Ge Changgao wants the security of old arrangements; Ge Qing wants small boat households to share freight work. They dispute livelihoods and risk, not ownership of the whole lake by decree. Wild Goose can protect cargo ashore and Qingfu can settle payments; each partnership also raises questions of loss.

Visitors may ask schedules, negotiate carriage or take temporary work without joining. Crew members learn signals, follow the duty pilot and leave ballast and cargo order alone. Access to a hold does not open guild accounts. Salt-route conflict and storms encourage caution, not automatic hostility to every unfamiliar skiff. Individual crews remember reliable conduct in difficult water. Extorting fees under the young leader’s name drives away even supporters of reform.

lanchuan-o18.name: Crimson Hearth Manor — Organization
lanchuan-o18.content:
(Glacial Crags of Frost Ridge in the far north)
The realm's foremost swordsmithing foundry. Old Manor Lord Yan Hanlu is covered in burn scars and temperamental as forged iron, swearing: "Not an edge shall be granted for ten thousand gold to those lacking virtue." His granddaughter Yan Ji swings a heavy iron sledgehammer, determined to send prized blades out of the mountains in exchange for food and clothing. In the rear courtyard furnace, the unfinished broken sword "Half-Inch Frost" from nineteen years ago remains bone-chillingly cold.

lanchuan-o19.name: Lichun Opera Troupe
lanchuan-o19.content:
(Ancestral home in Jinxi, Qinchuan; autumn tour in Sangma Town, Sihuai)
A century-old lineage fusing opera and martial arts. Troupe Master Bai Henian sings the righteous old-man roles with resonant vigor, while martial dan Hong Xiao's lightning-fast kicks swirl impenetrable as wind and rain. On stage, the actors draw no sharpened edges, but once out of costume, every one of them wields lethal short-range brawling skills, secretly carrying covert messages for heroes of every path.

lanchuan-o20.name: Cold Mountain Hunting Guild
lanchuan-o20.content:
(Cold Pine Fort Stronghold in Frost Ridge)
A living map of the extreme northern snow plains. Guildmaster Lei Baishan upholds mountain codes like iron law, while female guide Lan Xue treads over snow without leaving a trace. Upon the frost-locked peaks, merchant caravans and escort riders would not survive half a day without their longbows and sleds.

lanchuan-o21.name: Zhenhai Martial Arts Hall
lanchuan-o21.content:
(Great Wharf of Lankou City)
The unyielding backbone of the coastal commoners. Hall Master Guan Shanhai hails from the outer disciples of Mount Tai, blending Daiyue Fist with the grappling arts of seafaring fishermen to create the Zhenhai Fist. He accepts students regardless of lineage, judging only by their strength. Eldest Disciple Zheng Tieniu runs the challenge ring all day, helping dock laborers forge a rugged frame for self-defense.

## Contacts and everyday life

Zhenhai School keeps its courtyard through dockside tuition. Guan Shanhai blends the stances learned as an outer Mount Tai student with sailors’ close grappling. Zheng Tieniu runs practice; many pupils must still feed families after work. Old Mount Tai contacts are not authority over that school, nor does Guan’s friendship with Gu Huaiyuan make every pupil answer for the salt gang.

Teaching starts with health, injuries, the lesson offered and available time. Poor pupils may negotiate work for instruction without pledging lifelong service. Sparring needs agreement on force and stops for injury; one victory is not complete transmission. Street bullying under the school’s name draws distinct reactions from victims and classmates. Helping an opponent up and paying for broken furniture protects the livelihood the fists were meant to defend.

lanchuan-r01.name: Lankou
lanchuan-r01.content:
**Overview**: A vital estuary hub where the Lanchuan River meets the sea, laden with salty sea breezes and the deafening roar of crashing waves. Beyond the city walls lie blinding white brine flats, while inside, the merchant-packed Qingfu Guild bank bustles with activity. Behind Tidewatch Cliff, the Mount Tai Sect maintains its Eastern Peak Lodge, while disciples of the Zhenhai Martial Arts Hall scrape a living along the docks. The folk are candid yet meticulous down to the penny: wine can be had on credit for three days, but on the fourth day, someone will surely arrive at your door to settle the score.

## Life and paths through the region

Salt-flat channels, city remittances and the lamps at Tidewatch Cliff serve some of the same boats, but each has different owners. Swimmers can survey shallows, negotiators can compare old tide marks, and literate visitors can ask about disputed payments. Work and payment require a local agreement. A mediated boundary, a new channel and a violent clash leave different circumstances rather than the same pursuit.

The cliff lamp has lately appeared a quarter-hour earlier than boatmen remember, while the tide board still bears its old date. Mud lines at the salt flats and the keeper below the cliff offer independent evidence. Correcting the signal, marking a detour or declining the work can settle this local trouble without inventing an enemy behind every event.

lanchuan-r02.name: Qingping Lake
lanchuan-r02.content:
**Overview**: An eight-hundred-li expanse of misty waters and lush water grass. Returning Wild Goose Peak of the Mount Heng Sect sits south of the lake, where the misty river clouds blend seamlessly with the water fortresses of the boat gangs. This land yields water caltrops, fine fish, and mellow wine, but also conceals countless river pirates and hidden sect sentries. Its martial artists favor short weapons and naval warfare, appearing refined and leisurely in deportment, but striking with relentless, yielding subtlety.

## Life and paths through the region

Boat repair at Hedu, fish trading at Duckweed Dock, lodging at Three Willows and the closed gates of Mistwater Manor give the lake several livelihoods. A chart helps locate an old inlet but cannot replace the current water level. One passage, net repair or escort can start a boating career without winning control of a gang.

The Chang Geng wreck's blade marks, burned ledger and witnesses' remembered wind must be compared. Cutting a cable to survive does not prove murder; rescuing someone from a fire does not erase cargo debts. A discovered layer can have its own resolution. Delivering an old belonging need not reunite all seven friends or force reconciliation.

lanchuan-r03.name: Sihuai
lanchuan-r03.content:
**Overview**: A sprawling plain where the Grand Canal meets the Yangtze River, bustling with dense traffic of carriages and a forest of ship masts. This is the bedrock of the Beggar Sect, the realm's greatest faction, as well as the central hive where the Rain-Listening Pavilion gathers news from all quarters. Opera troupes pitch their stages here, porters sweat under heavy loads, and people of every walk of life intermingle. It boasts the richest urban atmosphere, the fastest-traveling rumors, and the easiest spark to whip a calm lake into towering waves.

## Life and paths through the region

Qinghe embroiderers, Canal Market porters and Old Locust beggars each know a different stretch of river. Ask whoever handled a missing object; inspect cargo and agree on sailing time and payment before escorting it. Cant can reduce misunderstanding and movement skills help inspect a bank, but neither supplies another person's testimony.

An old bowl and incomplete palm prints lead toward the sealed-palm affair. Knowing a name does not confer instruction. Visitors can pass sourced evidence to a willing listener, seek a teacher or live by skills already learned. One elder refusing an interview closes his testimony, not every possibility in Sihuai.

lanchuan-r04.name: Mount Shaoshi
lanchuan-r04.content:
**Overview**: Lofty mountains rising across the Central Plains, paved with ancient green stone. Shaolin Temple, the thousand-year ancestral court of Chan Buddhism, rests at the base of Mount Shaoshi, while the main altar of the Mount Song Sect, leader of the Five Mountains Sword Sects, dominates Victorious View Peak on Mount Taishi across the ridge. Here, Buddhist chants interweave with the ring of drawn swords. Farmers till temple fields below, while mountain passes and checkpoints enforce rigorous inspections. Jianghu travelers who arrive here invariably slow their pace, holding their breath in hushed reverence.

## Life and paths through the region

The mill outside the temple and wheat carts from Maihuang need reliable legs; the copying room needs patience; formal sparring has its own courtesies. Visiting a temple is not joining a school. Lodging, asking directions and carrying grain need not enlist a traveler in the rivalry between sects.

Blank portions of a pagoda rubbing can be checked against repaired stone and old copying paper rather than seized by defeating its keeper. An old agreement proves only what its surviving words say. Recognition and interpretation still require a conversation with those involved. Restraint, escorting companions and checking rumors are worthwhile growth alongside martial strength.

lanchuan-r05.name: Mount Taihe
lanchuan-r05.content:
**Overview**: A renowned mountain in Jingchu, its seventy-two peaks piercing the sky like bamboo shoots. The sacred seat of the True Martial Great Emperor, it is home to the Mount Wudang Sect, the sanctuary of internal martial arts. Here, Daoist Master Zhang Sanfeng founded the world-shaking art of Taiji. Below the mountain, tea fragrance greets the senses; halfway up, white clouds lock the peaks, and Daoist temples cascade along the slopes. The people are modest and gentle, leaving generous leeway in speech, yet in true combat, the soft-overcoming-hard force of Taiji can shatter the bones of any reckless assailant.

## Life and paths through the region

Tea merchants at Yingxian, old bushes on Cloudmist Slope and porters climbing Hundred-Step Stair move at different speeds. Study inner practice, survey a tea trail, deliver a letter or rent a quiet room. Work and cultivation take their own time; a good deed below a famous mountain does not buy a supreme technique.

The old man at Heartwashing Stream avoids a history he is not ready to own, not every visitor. When shown a bowl, handwritten notes or testimony, he can identify what he recognizes and what he does not. One answered question may end quietly. Regret does not require a new ambush.

lanchuan-r06.name: Cangwu Ridge
lanchuan-r06.content:
**Overview**: The strategic key to Guanzhong, sheer cliffs soaring thousands of fathoms. The Mount Hua Sect, masters of the realm's most perilous precipice, perches atop Jade Maiden Peak and Morning Sun Peak, with Yue Buqun's title as the "Gentleman Sword" celebrated throughout the passes. The trails are treacherous and narrow, clouds locking deep chasms, with the herb-gathering healers of Rejuvenation Hall midway up and iron chains lining the cliff paths. The folk here bear the cold, hardened resolve of the northwest; swords are drawn at the slightest provocation, their techniques vicious, strange, and perilous, treading on the brink of the void with every stride.

## Life and paths through the region

Iron-Bridge Station lives by keeping a route open, Springreturn Valley by herbs and medicine, and Jinxi by caring for travelers. Companions must agree before crossing; medicine has a seller and source. Gathering an herb, recognizing a poison and knowing treatment are different abilities. Examine an old prescription and the water at Mistlock Ravine's edge before entering.

A correction in an old casebook and traces of testing provide separate clues. Establishing a changed formula explains one failed batch, not malicious intent by every healer. Help the current patient, seek the original record or take evidence to a trusted practitioner. Becoming master of the valley is optional.

lanchuan-r07.name: Yanbei
lanchuan-r07.content:
**Overview**: Outside the Great Wall, yellow sand stings the face beneath boundless gray skies and vast wilderness. Outside Falling Goose Pass, merchant caravans and camel bells stretch unending, where frontier oases gaze out toward broken stone beacon towers. The ancient Hanging Nunnery of the Northern Sacred Peak Mount Heng Sect is embedded into cliffs thousands of fathoms high, its Buddhist chants below Nature-Perceiving Peak delivering the souls of the battlefield dead. Here, long spears, stiff bows, steed mounts, and short blades reign supreme; the folk are blunt and fierce, their words hitting like blowing sand, holding fast to keeping promises and wiping away old grudges over a shared bowl of wine.

## Life and paths through the region

Falling-Goose Pass checks cargo, Camelbell Market trades water, Blackstone Station negotiates escorts and Sand-Spring Village worries about its animals. Horsemanship, weapon repair and escort work all matter. Check whether a water stop remains usable before taking a shortcut. An inexperienced traveler may accompany an ordinary caravan leg without talking away storms or supply needs.

Empty water skins may reflect torn seams, short measures or water shared en route. Stitching, transactions and separate memories provide evidence. Resolve one loss without blaming every frontier dispute on one gang. Declining an escort leaves study, trade and work inside the pass available.

lanchuan-r08.name: Frost Ridge
lanchuan-r08.content:
**Overview**: Swirling snowdrifts and frozen rivers lock the mountains. Serving as the corridor linking the north to the far western plateau, it is home to the Mount Kunlun Sect's snow mountain lodge and Crimson Hearth Manor, the premier smithing clan of the northern lands. Cold gales slice like knives while iron forges spew flame day and night. This land yields the realm's toughest Kunlun cold iron, along with fine bows and frost-forged swords. Hunters track snow foxes across frozen ranges while smiths swing hundred-catty sledgehammers. The folk are sparing with words, but brush the snow from your coat as you enter, and the host will surely pour you a piping bowl of fiery Xin Family Circulating Liquor.

## Life and paths through the region

Coldpine Fort knows the snow line, Redfurnace Manor its furnaces, Ling River Ferry its ice, and Snowlistening Lodge whom it will receive. Fine cold iron does not guarantee correct tempering. Learn smithing by inspection, preparation and an actual repair; prose cannot turn a broken blade into a legendary weapon. Warm clothing, food and a credible route matter beyond the snow line. Stopping can be sound judgment.

Cracks confined to a furnace's final batch point toward fuel, quenching order and handover records before sabotage. Admitting a mistake may yield more careful cooperation rather than a feud. A winter home, a practiced craft and a kept promise can be meaningful northern ambitions.

lanchuan-c01.name: Half-Scroll Taoist Canon
lanchuan-c01.content:
* **Character Background**: You are a registered lay disciple at Zixiao Palace on Mount Taihe, nominally taken under the wing of Yu Lianzhou, the Second Hero of Wudang. However, the one who usually guides your training at the monastery is Yunshu, a Daoist nun a few years your senior. You have thoroughly mastered the breathing exercises in the opening pages of the *Twofold Polarities Qi-Nourishing Art* and can cycle your boxing stances into seamless circles, but the moment you trade a palm strike with an ordinary bladesman down the mountain, it becomes clear your inner energy is still shallow and far from mature. According to the monastery's rules, registered disciples must travel down the mountain before the Double Ninth Festival to experience mundane worldly life before it is decided whether they will formally don the Daoist robes, take vows, and enter the inner mountain.
* **Starting Location**: Mount Taihe · Yingxian Town (in front of the tea merchant's shop).
* **Existing Connections**:
  * **Yu Lianzhou**: Your master in name only. Stern and austere, he speaks rarely, only occasionally offering pointers such as, "The essence of the fist lies not in speed, but in staying unhurried."
  * **Yunshu**: The senior sister who tempers your sinews and bones. Gentle on the outside yet unyielding within, she never scolds you when you slack off during practice, merely pouring you a bowl of warm tea in silence.
  * **Tu Dahu**: The chief manager of the Yingxian Town tea firm. Trained in Quanzhen Daoist medicine, he always saves large steamed white buns for Wudang juniors descending the mountain and frequently sends them on errands to deliver tea.
* **Plausible Belongings**: A Wudang registered disciple wooden token (carved with the Taiji Yin-Yang pattern), a coarse slate-grey hemp Daoist robe, an outer-sect handwritten transcript of *Twofold Polarities Qi-Nourishing Art: Annotations* (the first half only), an ordinary green-steel longsword, and thirty copper cash.
* **Advantage**: Along both the land and water routes of Mount Taihe and Qingping Lake, people recognize your Daoist robes. You can lodge at tea shops and Daoist branch courtyards, or pass messages up to Zixiao Palace.
* **Tether**: You must return to Zixiao Palace before the Double Ninth Festival in the ninth month to report to Master Song Yuanqiao, conclude your leave of absence, and account for what you saw down the mountain. Even more, you want to uncover what unresolved grudge Shen Guhe—who sits alone every day cradling his sword in the Lone Pine Pavilion halfway up the Hundred-Step Stairway—actually holds against your sect.

> **Opening Scene**
>
> The long street of Yingxian Town remains shrouded in thin mist, the flagstone road radiating the damp chill of late autumn. The tea shop has barely removed its first shutter-board when shopkeeper Tu Dahu brings a steaming, coarse-porcelain sea-bowl out from the back hall, thrusting it into your hands without room for refusal.
>
> "Drink it while it's hot. Old ginger, brown sugar, and brown rice broth—wards off the cold." He pats the tea dust from his apron and shoves two firm steamed buns into your chest. "Second Master Yu sent a Daoist novice down last night with word that you are to stay below until the Double Ninth. No set destination, no assigned errand—just told you to keep an extra pair of eyes open on the streets. In the jianghu, you can't push your way to fame merely by practicing palm forms on a stone courtyard."
>
> You lower your head and swallow a mouthful of hot broth, its sweet, peppery warmth scalding down your throat. Looking up, the three thousand blue-stone steps of the Hundred-Step Stairway vanish tier by tier into the depths of mid-altitude white clouds. Beneath the Lone Pine Pavilion jutting out alone halfway up the mountain sits the faint outline of a desolate figure. That iron sword wrapped in white cloth rests across his knees, like a dead rock rooted into the cliff face.
>
> Tu Dahu glances along your line of sight and sighs: "That Daoist Master Shen has been sitting in that pavilion for four full days now. A pot of wild mountain tea at dawn, two cold flatbreads at dusk—no one can coax him to budge. The whole town whispers he's a fiend come to kick down the Wudang gate, but what sort of fiend sits out in the wind and endures four days of freezing cold?"
>
> The Wudang wooden token at your hip clinks gently against the scabbard with your stride. Farther down the street, several porters peddling mountain goods are arguing with a shop clerk until red in the face over a difference of two copper cash. At the town dock, a ferry bound for Qingping Lake rings its iron bell, the work chants calling for passengers rising louder with every cry.
>
> Tu Dahu gives you a shove: "Go on. East or west, just get back to town before nightfall, and you won't lack for a piping-hot bowl of noodles."

lanchuan-c02.name: A Bowl of Escort Rice
lanchuan-c02.content:
* **Character Background**: You are an escort runner from a humble background in the Wildgoose Escort Agency of Qingping Lake. You know how to sink into a sturdy square horse stance, how to shout the escort cry "He-wu!" at the top of your raspy lungs, and how to tell in the dead of night from the rustle of wind through horse manes which mule's iron horseshoe has come loose. This iron-spined goose-feather saber was drawn from the agency's armory; the leather bracers on your wrists have been scuffed and mended again and again; and every stroke and parry of your saber craft was learned through beatings along two thousand leagues of windblown, dusty escort routes. You have no renowned, great sect behind you—only the golden wild goose spreading its wings upon the escort banner.
* **Starting Location**: Qingping Lake · Hedu Town (the rear courtyard of the Wildgoose Escort Agency headquarters).
* **Existing Connections**:
  * **Huo Qianli**: Chief Escort of the agency, formerly one of the Seven Companions of Lanchuan. With hawk-like eyes, he remembers every life-or-death run you've ever walked—and the eight taels of settlement silver you took in advance.
  * **Yan Xiaowu**: A young runner of your cohort. Sharp-tongued and fleet-footed, he always tries to drag you into trouble with him, but he never bolts first when facing highwaymen.
  * **Chai Feng**: The veteran escort who took you on your first journey into the northern desert wastes. Now retired at the Broken Beacon Platform in Yanbei, his letter sent back via a merchant caravan last month bore only a single sentence: "The well water has turned bitter."
* **Plausible Belongings**: An iron-spined goose-feather saber (an old agency piece), polished brass-buckled leather bracers, a cast-bronze escort whistle, travel documents and permits bearing the vermilion seal of the Wildgoose Escort Agency, a pack of fried-flour rations, and a gourd of fiery shaojiu.
* **Advantage**: You have old agency acquaintances across post houses, cart lodges, and docks along land and water. Changing horses and finding lodging is exceedingly easy, and you catch wind of bandit movements along the official highways two days faster than the average traveler.
* **Tether**: The eight taels of advance silver must be paid off slowly through escort runs; Chai Feng's baffling note about the "bitter well water" remains like a thorn stuck in your chest.

> **Opening Scene**
>
> The morning light over Hedu Town is sliced open by the dull whistling of blades cleaving the air. On the yellow-dirt training ground of the Wildgoose Escort Agency's rear yard, thirty or forty bare-chested runners hold horse stances, their steel sabers chopping violently into rot-wood posts wrapped in raw sheet iron, jarring old tiles on the yard walls until puffs of dust shower down.
>
> You have just dumped two buckets of well water into the horse trough when Yan Xiaowu bumps hard into your back. Chewing on half a fried dough stick, he drops his voice mysteriously: "Hey, heard the news? The outside world's in an uproar. They're saying that while crossing the Ten-Mile Embankment two days ago, our agency lost a crate of imperial celadon porcelain bound for the official kilns in Qinghe City!"
>
> "Lost it?" You wipe the splash of well water from your face.
>
> "Lost my foot!" Yan Xiaowu sneers. "The mule hauling the cart was just spooked by a water snake in the reeds, the wheel jolted in a mud hole, and a speck of green glaze no bigger than a mung bean chipped off the corner of a crate. Those busybodies who love a spectacle managed to spin a chipped corner into our escort being looted by forest brigands!"
>
> Before his words finish falling, three sharp, hurried clangs ring out from the iron cloud-gong behind the entrance hall's spirit wall. This is the summons for Chief Escort Huo Qianli himself taking the roll call.
>
> Passing through the vestibule, you see Huo Qianli standing beneath the eaves with hands behind his back. His gaze sweeps over the faces of dozens of disciples like a merchant weighing gold, finally settling upon yours.
>
> "Regarding the run to the porcelain shop in Qinghe City: the merchant refuses to let the matter rest and has added a covert escort tally, demanding delivery strictly within twelve days." Huo Qianli's voice is not loud, yet heavy as raw pig iron. "Who will escort the secondary cart on this route? If you run into the Songshan Sect searching the passes along the way, you are only permitted to present your travel papers. Under no circumstances may you draw your blades."
>
> He slaps a vermilion tally slip bearing a wild goose feather onto the table. The chopping wood sounds in the yard pause in unison. Recalling the silver you owe, and Chai Feng's crooked, ragged letter from the northern frontier, you take a step forward and reach out to take the tally.

lanchuan-c03.name: Visitor at the Ferry
lanchuan-c03.content:
* **Character Background**: You possess neither high martial lineage nor the backing of an illustrious sect, nor do you know any palm techniques or sword forms that shake the martial world. For the past three years, you have worked as an odd-job laborer on a black-awning salt smuggler's boat sailing out of Lankou City—sculling the oars, swabbing the decks, and holding off water bandits. Last month, the old boat master died abruptly from a sea chill, and the salt gang seized the battered boat as collateral. You packed your bundle and left the craft. Apart from three coarse flatbreads, you carry only a sealed letter pressed into your hands by the old master before his last breath, with strict instructions to deliver it overland to the Lianghuai region and hand it to a young Beggar Sect porter named Pu Xiaoqi.
* **Starting Location**: Lankou · Tidewatch Ferry (ferryman Song Laolu's dilapidated thatched shack).
* **Existing Connections**:
  * **Song Laolu**: An old boatman who has ferried at Tidewatch Ferry for decades. He took you in to sleep on his dirt floor for half a month, puffing dry tobacco day after day watching the tides rise and fall, never prying into your background.
  * **Lan Ali**: A brisk fisherwoman who leads White Egret Fishing Village. She once traded with you for several bags of contraband ballast salt. Knowing your strong swimming skills, she often calls you over to the village entrance for a bowl of mixed-fish soup.
* **Plausible Belongings**: A rawhide envelope securely sealed with black wax, a heavy oiled-cloth straw cape, a nine-foot raw hemp rope fitted with a three-pronged iron grapple, a fire-striker, and a rusty short utility knife for self-defense.
* **Advantage**: Thoroughly versed in waterways and swimming, familiar with river shallows, sandbars, and submerged reefs. You can exchange manual labor for meals at ferry crossings and docks, and vagrants of the jianghu harbor very little wariness toward you.
* **Tether**: The old boat master owed Pu Xiaoqi unpaid wages before he died, and this confidential letter feels heavy as a thousand catties. Whether it hides ancient grudges or hidden wealth, you have never broken the seal.

> **Opening Scene**
>
> Dusk at Tidewatch Ferry carries the thick, briny tang of seawater. Across the river, a few scattered lights flicker faintly, like stars dropped into pooled ink.
>
> Song Laolu sits on a stone mooring bollard by the shore, tapping his battered brass pipe bowl against the sole of his shoe. Without turning his head, he knows it is you purely from the steady rhythm of your footsteps: "That tatty leather letter... still tucked against your chest?"
>
> You press the stiff oilcloth bundle against your ribs and nod.
>
> "Old Zhao was tighter with his ledger than anyone while alive, yet on his deathbed he went and trusted an outsider lad like you." Song Laolu slowly exhales a puff of choking dry smoke. "The waters at the Lianghuai Grand Canal Junction run deep. The Clean Clothes faction masters of the Beggar Sect hold their noses high in the air; if you want to find Pu Xiaoqi, you'll have to dig through the muck heaps. Once the letter is delivered, pass along a message for me: tell him this ferryman's brittle bones haven't fallen apart yet, so quit smuggling salt toward the river mouth."
>
> Beneath the eaves, an old oiled-paper umbrella with two broken bamboo ribs sways gently in the sea breeze, the character *Qing* carved on its handle worn faint and white. In the tea shed, several contraband salt peddlers waiting for the morning tide lower their voices, discussing rumors that Gu Huaiyuan of the Green Salt Flats is about to close the shores and butcher people again.
>
> "The water's swift tonight; the big ferry departs at the fifth watch." Song Laolu jams his punt pole into the mud and slowly gets to his feet. "If you're scared, you can live in this rotten shack your whole life; this old man can always spare you half a bowl of thin congee. But the road is of your own choosing. Once you lift your foot, don't look back."
>
> You gaze out at the pitch-black Lanchuan River as its waters surge eastward without end. Tightening the oiled straw cape around your frame, you step out onto the slick gangplank.

---

lanchuan-w01.name: Lanchuan: The World and the Era
lanchuan-w01.brief_description: Lanchuan: The World and the Era.
lanchuan-w01.content:
# Chapter 1: The World and the Era

## 1.1 Name of the World

**Lanchuan**. When people speak of the "Lanchuan Jianghu," they refer to everything and everyone within a thousand leagues along both banks of the Lanchuan River. Originating in the far-western snowy plateaus, the Lanchuan River cuts through mountain passes and deep gorges, racing eastward until its momentum gathers into the Eastern Sea. Its waters connect north and south in all directions, binding great sects and common market folk into the very same watery web.

## 1.2 Player-Facing Summary

Flowing from west to east, the Lanchuan River winds through desert bastions, thousand-fathom precipices, tea-smoke-veiled Daoist temples, and eight hundred leagues of lakes and marshes, only reaching the sea at the river mouth. Ferries ply the waters, inns line the shores; travelers of the martial world gather in taverns to ask about the storms outside, while shopkeepers busy themselves over ledgers calculating yesterday's firewood and rice.

The bells of the Shaolin Temple carry for ten leagues; Daoists on Mount Wudang stand in morning stances along the cliffs; merchants of the Ming Cult's Five Elements Banners drive their camel caravans in silence through the gravel wastes; disciples of the Five Sacred Mountains Sword Sects gallop along official post roads to deliver merger notices. No matter how grand a figure's reputation, descending the mountain still requires finding a place to drink tea and eat noodles; no matter how brilliant a swordsman's art, crossing the river still requires paying three copper cash according to the rules. Here lie escort agencies with centuries of heritage, fishing families scraping by with two torn nets, and rough men who draw steel over a single cross word. The jianghu waits for no one, nor does it turn anyone away. Which road you tread and which door you enter first depend entirely on your own stride.

## 1.3 General Temperament of the Jianghu

* **The Marketplace Precedes the Grandmaster.** Walking the roads of Lanchuan, an innkeeper first checks whether you produce copper cash or broken silver, and a tavern waiter first asks how many ounces of shaojiu to ladle, only then glancing to see whether a longsword or a short saber hangs at your hip. Regardless of a sect leader's towering renown, there will always be someone down the mountain keeping strict accounts of their firewood, rice, oil, salt, ferry fares, and land rents.
* **Open Waterways, Wandering Grudges.** The main artery of the Lanchuan River connects with the Grand Canal and Qingping Lake; bulk shipments of medicinal herbs, salt, pelts, and covert arms intelligence mostly travel by water. Whoever controls the docks holds the sects by the throat.
* **Every Faction Earns Its Bread by Craft.** Shaolin relies on incense offerings and temple fields; Wudang leans on tea plantations and herb mountains; Beggar Sect brothers heave crates and shoulder loads at the Grand Canal Junction; Ming Cult branch altars hide within commercial caravans and workshops; sword-smiths rely on iron, while escort runners bet their lives. In the eyes of commoners, practicing martial arts is not about vaulting over roofs, but first and foremost a sturdy trade to put food in one's bowl.
* **Right, Wrong, and the Curse of Vain Glory.** The liveliest place in the martial world is rarely the dueling arena, but rather beneath the storyteller's table in a teahouse. A minor altercation passed across three ferry docks can warp into a blood feud between two entire sects.

## 1.4 Current Situation: Deep Autumn of the 23rd Year of Ninghe

Events begin in **early September of the 23rd Year of Ninghe**, around the Double Ninth Festival. Far to the north, the imperial court is consumed by provincial taxation and border defense, possessing neither the time nor the will to meddle in jianghu strife. While the martial realm appears tranquil on the surface, several massive undercurrents are crashing together:

1. **The Five Sacred Mountains Merger Storm**: Zuo Lengchan, leader of the Songshan Sect, secretly gathers experts under the pretext of countering the Demonic Cult. He dispatches his First Taibao, Ding Mian "The Tower-Supporting Hand," and Second Taibao, Fei Bin "The Great Songyang Hand," to provoke disputes on all sides, relentlessly cornering the Huashan, Hengshan, Mount Tai, and Mount Heng sects to force a unified alliance under his control.
2. **Huashan's Sword-Qi Schism and Thought-Refection Cliff**: Yue Buqun, the "Gentleman Sword," strictly disciplines his disciples, fretting day and night over his sect's decline and Songshan's encroaching pressure. His eldest disciple, Linghu Chong, has been confined to Thought-Reflection Cliff for consorting with heterodox figures while drinking, stirring up rampant rumors down the mountain.
3. **Liu Zhengfeng's Golden Basin Hand-Washing**: Liu Zhengfeng of the Hengshan Sect has quietly circulated invitations, setting the date after the Double Ninth Festival to wash his hands in a golden basin and retire from the martial world. Sect Leader Master Mo Da drifts about like a ghost, his stance murky and unfathomable.
4. **Shadow War between the Ming Cult and the Six Major Sects**: Following the battle at Bright Summit in the Western Regions, Zhang Wuji, the new cult leader, strives to dissolve old enmities. Yet Princess Shaomin, Zhao Min, commands experts from the imperial court and princely estates to lurk within the jianghu and stoke discord. Five Elements Banner members and Mongolian martial artists are frequently spotted near the foot of Mount Shaoshi, putting the Shaolin Disciplinary Hall on high alert.
5. **The Mystery of the Shaolin Sutra Pavilion Theft**: Whispers leak from the depths of the Bodhidharma Hall and the Sutra Pavilion that ancient scrolls have been tampered with. Abbot Xuanci orders the monastery gates tightened, while the guest-welcoming monk Xuzhu conducts quiet inspections of armed travelers along the street before the temple.
6. **The Taiji Dispute of Mount Wudang**: In recent years, Zhang Sanfeng has been in secluded meditation contemplating the ultimate principles of Taiji, leaving his senior disciple Song Yuanqiao to oversee general affairs. However, Shen Guhe, an estranged disciple who departed a decade ago, has declared he will return on the Double Ninth to challenge the mountain with his sword, testing whether Taiji can truly be used for slaughter.
7. **The Lianghuai Waterway Split within the Beggar Sect**: Porters and Beggar Sect members gather in ever-greater numbers at the Lianghuai Grand Canal Junction. Vice Chief Chen Youliang and the Stick-Wielding Elder clash openly and behind the scenes over sect rules and the distribution of grain and funds.
8. **Coastal Salt Routes and Dock Turf Wars**: Gu Huaiyuan, head of the contraband salt ring at the Green Salt Flats, has cordoned off the mudflats, preventing fishermen from casting nets and stalling the accounts of the city's Qingfu Guild.

**The Imperial Court's Stance**: The Ninghe dynasty maintains only local patrol inspectorates across prefectures to check city gate travel permits, collect state monopoly taxes, and round up petty thieves. As for the bloody feuds and blade-crossings between renowned sects and rogue outlaws, officials mostly turn a blind eye and a deaf ear; so long as it does not boil over into brazen robberies of official silver in broad daylight, the matters are left entirely to the rules of the jianghu.

## 1.5 Life of the Common Folk

* **Fishing Villages and Farming Hamlets**: Living at the mercy of the elements. River-mouth fishermen time their nets by the tides; wheat-hamlet tenants reap by the solar terms. They know no profound martial arts, but if anyone tramples a furrow of crops or kicks over a basket of fish, they will just as quickly take up carrying poles to fight for their lives.
* **Townspeople and Burghers**: Tea shop keepers, shoulder-pole porters, bookkeepers, and blacksmiths. In their eyes, martial artists are either free-spending customers prone to trouble, or jinxes who shatter tables and benches the moment a fight breaks out.
* **Inns and Pawnshops**: Waystations of martial world intelligence. Innkeepers have uncanny memories, needing only half a glance to reckon how many coins are left in your pouch; pawnshop appraisers are stone-faced and ruthless, refusing to advance the price of half a bowl of plain noodles for a snapped blade.

## 1.6 Circumstances and Livelihoods of Martial Practitioners

Martial artists across the land generally fall into three categories:
* **Sect Scions**: Under the banner of Shaolin, Wudang, Emei, the Five Sacred Mountains, or the Ming Cult. Sheltered by elders and supported by estate revenues, they are equally shackled by strict sect codes; stepping out into the world on business means constantly shouldering their "sect's reputation."
* **Trade Professionals**: Escort masters, boatmen, herbalists, blacksmiths, and constables. Martial skill is the breadwinner hidden at the bottom of their chests; dull blades must be whetted, severe wounds must be nursed, and with every journey, wear and tear must be calculated to the copper.
* **Drifting Outlaws**: Sectless and wandering across ferry docks and open markets. Guarding manors, escorting small consignments, carrying messages, or providing street muscle. Debts of gratitude pile up coin by coin, and every bowl of thin gruel is bought with their own two fists.

## 1.7 Travel, Board, and Social Customs

* **Money**: Daily transactions use copper cash and strings of cash; substantial expenses call for broken silver and cast ingots. A night in a woodshed costs a few dozen cash; a bowl of aged-broth noodles runs a few coppers. What is truly precious is a renowned physician's wound balm and a smith's fine steel.
* **Pace of Travel**: Walking overland on two legs, covering fifty to sixty leagues in a day marks a strong walker. Horses are fast, but on the precipices of Mount Shaoshi or the plank paths of Mount Hua, they are far less reliable than straw sandals. Traveling downriver by water with the wind in your sails can double your speed, but when fighting headwinds and counter-currents, progress depends step by step on trackers hauling the towline.
* **Lodging**: Inns are divided into common bunkhouses, standard private rooms, and detached courtyard suites. Guests pay a deposit upon entering; those without money must pawn belongings, and buying on credit requires a guarantee from a local figure of standing. Derelict temples and roadside tea sheds in the wild can also provide shelter, provided one knows the etiquette: never claim dry firewood that someone else has already gathered.
* **Information Channels**: News travels fastest via the carrier pigeons and bamboo slips of the Rain-Listening Tower, the secret argot calls of Beggar Sect disciples, and the water whistles of boat gangs. The tales told by teahouse storytellers are often watered down; while the names are usually correct, the inner details are embellished with colorful flourishes.

## 1.8 Martial Realms and Standards

Martial arts in this world fall into four relative realms, representing only an artist's seasoning and discernment within the jianghu, rather than rigid numerical system attributes:

* **First Glimpse of the Threshold**: Forms and routines are thoroughly drilled, sufficient to handle several common farmhands; inner energy is just taking root, barely enough to keep from panting heavily while traveling.
* **Entering the Hall**: Mastery of a martial style has become neat and precise, sufficient to serve as an escort runner in an agency or an instructor in a martial arts hall; inner breath can endure half a day of hard clashes.
* **Entering the Chamber**: Techniques have fused into natural instinct, qualifying one to be a core disciple in major sects or a formidable figure commanding a local greenwood territory; capable of facing ten opponents without fluster, knowing when to conserve strength and avoid danger.
* **The Pinnacle**: Giants of the generation such as Zhang Sanfeng, Xuanci, Zuo Lengchan, Yue Buqun, Master Miejue, and Zhang Wuji. Their discernment borders on the divine, lifting heavy burdens as if weightless; yet born of mortal flesh and blood, they still tire, can still fall victim to covert plots, and can still suffer grievous wounds.

## 1.9 Opening Scene: River Mouth at Dusk

> On the mudflats of Tidewatch Ferry, the autumn wind of the ebbing tide whips up a briny sea tang that makes one squint.
>
> Song Laolu grips an unlit brass pipe between his teeth, tying an unyielding knot around a rotting wooden bollard with a frayed raw-hemp mooring line. Across the river, only a few scattered lamps have been lit in Qinghe City, but in the ferry tea shed, several contraband salt peddlers are already slamming tables and shouting at the server over a single copper coin of tea money.
>
> At the adjacent table, a porter clad in oiled-cloth work clothes spits out a mouthful of tea dregs and lowers his voice: "Heard the news? Trouble's brewing at the foot of Mount Shaoshi. Fei Bin, the Second Taibao of the Songshan Sect, has blocked the official highway with dozens of men, claiming an ancestral scroll of Patriarch Bodhidharma was stolen from the Shaolin Sutra Pavilion. Not a single traveler carrying a blade is allowed northward!"
>
> An old man beside him carrying empty baskets sneers: "Shaolin loses a sutra, and what business is that of the Songshan Sect? Over these past two years, Alliance Leader Zuo has shoved that Five Mountains command banner straight toward the incense burners of other people's temples."
>
> The hearth fire flickers, and the sea wind rustles the tattered thatched shed. You press your hand against the parcel in your breast. The tea still scalds your tongue, but out on the mudflats, the boatmaster is already shouting for passengers in his raspy, cracked voice.

---

lanchuan-life-identity.name: Backgrounds and a life of one’s own
lanchuan-life-identity.brief_description: The ferry traveller, escort worker and registered Daoist student are equally valid backgrounds, not ranks on one prescribed road.
lanchuan-life-identity.content:
The ferry traveller, escort worker and registered Daoist student are equally valid backgrounds, not ranks on one prescribed road. Apprenticeship, acquaintances and experience follow the identity actually chosen; another person’s letter, work or obligation does not transfer to them.

One may carry a letter or decline, practise, earn a living, care for friends or change trades. The broken palm art, the Seven Friends’ past and making a home are possible concerns, not required routes. Completing one matter completes that matter alone. Nobody must reunite, rule or retire, and the world does not end there. Meals, directions and conversation need not all become commissions.

lanchuan-life-work.name: Schools, trades and money
lanchuan-life-work.brief_description: A school name, escort job or familiar face at the boat guild explains how people receive someone; it does not open scriptures, armouries, vessels or tills.
lanchuan-life-work.content:
A school name, escort job or familiar face at the boat guild explains how people receive someone; it does not open scriptures, armouries, vessels or tills. A lesson, favour or loan requires the person entitled to agree. Seeing a move, reading a page and learning to use it are different. Injuries matter, sparring needs agreed restraint, and a famous art does not make flesh immune to blades.

Growers protect a harvest, escorts their teams, exchanges their ability to pay, and teachers their own lessons. Goods, teaching and employment depend on availability and agreement. A quote is not payment and a plan is not a debt. Actual loans and transactions follow their terms. Friends may share meals, help or decline without charging interest on every meeting. A finished job can be followed by rest; work, learning and care all sustain a life.

lanchuan-life-news.name: How news travels and favours endure
lanchuan-life-news.brief_description: Tea-stall gossip, direct observation, a letter and a participant’s acknowledgement carry different weight.
lanchuan-life-news.content:
Tea-stall gossip, direct observation, a letter and a participant’s acknowledgement carry different weight. Informants have sources, mistakes and things left unsaid. Sharing a city does not share secrets. Private words first reach only those who heard them; letters must arrive and meetings require consent. An old object permits a question, not a decision about its owner’s beliefs or future.

Favours remain specific: one introduction is not permanent access, nor does one broken promise erase every prior tie. Passed time ages news, brings cargo dates closer and allows recovery. Without an agreed date, no deadly countdown appears from nowhere. Distant people continue their lives, but reports of deaths, changed territory or broken schools need actual messages or witnesses, not merely days without a player visit.

lanchuan-life-unfinished-paths.name: Discoveries, Answers and Your Own Road
lanchuan-life-unfinished-paths.brief_description: Local lives continue; an answer may end an affair or change a later encounter.
lanchuan-life-unfinished-paths.content:
A region supports work, visits, training, trade and travel without requiring an accepted task. A mystery begins with a concrete anomaly and traceable evidence. Following it should answer the original question. An ordinary, sad or partial answer is valid without another mastermind behind it.

Goals grow from circumstances: obtaining tools, learning a method, repairing a weapon, finding lodging or completing a trustworthy delivery. These can intersect without becoming a shared checklist or scheduled grind. A real completion leaves stable consequences; reopening it needs a new cause and contact.

A distant change is not automatically known. A received message, visit or investigation establishes what the player learns. Goodwill or caution belongs to the person expressing it. Refusal, rest and changing direction remain available. A resolved mystery does not reset through amnesia or repeated rewards.

lanchuan-p01.name: Song Laolu
lanchuan-p01.brief: The old ferryman who has rowed flatboats at Tidewatch Ferry for decades. Everyone who meets him must respectfully address him as Old Song. Beneath the eaves of his thatched hut hangs an old umbrella with broken ribs, which he never allows anyone to touch.
lanchuan-p01.role: Tidewatch Ferry · Old Ferryman; former veteran of the Surge Boat Gang, retired from the Jianghu for thirty years.

lanchuan-p02.name: Fan Shouzhuo
lanchuan-p02.brief: The chief manager overseeing the largest bank at the great river's estuary. His pet phrase is, "Allow this old man to calculate once more." Amid the dense shops of Lankou City, Chief Fan is the only one who can lend out a hundred taels of silver solely on the credit of a person's face.
lanchuan-p02.role: Lankou City · Chief Manager of the Qingfu Association.

lanchuan-p03.name: Su Xiaoman
lanchuan-p03.brief: The youngest and most agile clerk in the Qingfu Bank. Her fingers work the abacus faster than ordinary men can speak. Rumor has it that when provoked, she can fling abacus beads like iron pellets straight at an opponent's throat.
lanchuan-p03.role: Lankou City · Female Bookkeeping Apprentice of the Qingfu Association.

lanchuan-p04.name: Guan Shanhai
lanchuan-p04.brief: A famed martial arts master along the coast. He accepts apprentices without regard for pedigree or bone structure, testing first whether one can haul two buckets of seawater across half a li of mudflat in a single breath.
lanchuan-p04.role: Lankou City · Master of Zhenhai Martial Arts School; former outer-sect lay disciple of the Mount Tai Sect.

lanchuan-p05.name: Zheng Tieniu
lanchuan-p05.brief: The sturdy pillar among the school's younger generation. He possesses Herculean strength and fights with straightforward honesty in the ring, yet off the platform, he often pays out of his own pocket to treat beaten opponents to bowls of hearty pork noodles.
lanchuan-p05.role: Lankou City · Senior Disciple of Zhenhai Martial Arts School.

lanchuan-p06.name: Lan Ali
lanchuan-p06.brief: The most skilled swimmer across the mudflats, capable of holding her breath beneath deep waters for half an hour without surfacing. Whenever someone's net snags on reef rocks, she readily dives into the sea to haul it free.

lanchuan-p07.name: Gu Huaiyuan
lanchuan-p07.brief: An iron-fisted leader ruling over dozens of hectares of salt pans at Green Salt Beach. His "Tide-Severing Saber" is ruthless and overbearing; both black and white paths along the sea take the long way around him.
lanchuan-p07.role: Green Salt Beach · Illicit Salt Chieftain; Underworld Hegemon.

lanchuan-p08.name: Xu Zhu
lanchuan-p08.brief: The landlady of a cliffside inn who grills mouthwateringly aromatic spicy sea fish. Whenever someone probes for Jianghu secrets, she feigns deafness and plays dumb, claiming she is "old and forgetful."
lanchuan-p08.role: Wangchao Cliff · Proprietress of Wangchao Inn; former senior intelligence broker of Rain Listening Pavilion.

lanchuan-p09.name: Huo Qianli
lanchuan-p09.brief: The helmsman of the Wild Goose Escort Bureau, which spans land and water networks across the north and south. In twenty years of escorting shipments, he has never suffered a failure; he rarely smiles or jokes, earning the Jianghu epithet "Ten Thousand Li Without a Ripple."
lanchuan-p09.role: Hedu Town · Chief Escort of the Wild Goose Escort Bureau; one of the "Lanchuan Seven".

lanchuan-p10.name: Yan Xiaowu
lanchuan-p10.brief: The quickest-tongued, fastest-footed young scout in the bureau's rear yard. Gifted with superb lightness skill, not even the rustling of a leaf or blade of grass escapes his ears on the escort road.
lanchuan-p10.role: Hedu Town · Scout of the Wild Goose Escort Bureau.

lanchuan-p11.name: Ge Changgao
lanchuan-p11.brief: The veteran leader ruling over eight hundred li of waterways. Despite his limp, standing at the bow of a swaying wooden barge, he remains as steady and motionless as an iron anchor dropped into the deep.
lanchuan-p11.role: Duckweed Dock · Grand Helm Master of the Surge Boat Gang.

lanchuan-p12.name: Ge Qing
lanchuan-p12.brief: Only daughter of the old helm master, and leader of the younger boatmen on Qingping Lake. Her aquatic prowess surpasses her teacher's; she is dead set on distributing the profits of bulk water transport equally among scattered fishing households.
lanchuan-p12.role: Duckweed Dock · Junior Helm Master of the Surge Boat Gang.

lanchuan-p13.name: Auntie Zhong
lanchuan-p13.brief: Matriarch of Three Willows Inn, famed for her unparalleled wild duck porridge. In the rear courtyard of the inn, the premier guestroom remains bolted behind a massive iron padlock, unavailable for rent even if offered a hundred taels of gold.
lanchuan-p13.role: Three Willows Inn · Proprietress; one of the "Lanchuan Seven".

lanchuan-p14.name: Rong Jiugao
lanchuan-p14.brief: The supreme legend of the martial world across Qingping Lake. His swordsmanship borders on the divine. For twenty years, he has secluded himself on an isolated island manor in the lake, carving a stone tablet that announces to the world: "The Master Receives No Guests."
lanchuan-p14.role: Mist Wave Manor · Manor Lord; reclusive supreme sword master.

lanchuan-p15.name: Auntie Lian
lanchuan-p15.brief: A water-chestnut gathering woman of the village, exceptionally adept in water lore and capable of identifying a hundred varieties of rare aquatic medicinal herbs across Qingping Lake. The waterside tunes she hums are sorrowful yet gentle, deeply moving to the soul.
lanchuan-p15.role: Water-Chestnut Song Village · Water-chestnut harvester; folk herbalist.
lanchuan-p15.initial_place_label: Water-Chestnut Village and Foothills of Wild Goose Peak

lanchuan-p16.name: Xiang Danian
lanchuan-p16.brief: The most valued senior disciple of Liu Zhengfeng, the second-in-command of the Southern Peak's Mount Heng Sect. Recently, he has been shuttling between Qingping Lake and Returning Wild Goose Peak, helping his master organize the realm-shaking Golden Basin Hand-Washing Ceremony.
lanchuan-p16.role: Mount Heng Sect; eldest disciple under Liu Zhengfeng.
lanchuan-p16.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p17.name: Lu Youjiao
lanchuan-p17.brief: The current Chief of the Beggar Gang, the greatest sect in the world. Despite standing atop countless gangs, he sits year-round by the massive iron cauldron at Old Locust Dock, sharing bowls of mixed-grain porridge with common brothers at the grassroots.
lanchuan-p17.role: Old Locust Dock; Chief of the Beggar Gang; leader of the Dirty Clothes Faction.

lanchuan-p18.name: Chen Youliang
lanchuan-p18.brief: The most politically astute and influential elder among the Beggar Gang's younger generation. He controls docks, taxation profits, and canal laborer authority throughout the Lianghuai region, with disciples spread across major sects.
lanchuan-p18.role: Old Locust Dock; Beggar Gang Eight-Bag Executive Elder; leader of the Clean Clothes Faction.

lanchuan-p19.name: Niu Bushi
lanchuan-p19.brief: The gang's oldest and most stubborn veteran. Boasts that he hasn't done an honest day of work in his life and built his name purely on begging; detests disciples of the Clean Clothes Faction wearing silks and colors.
lanchuan-p19.role: Old Locust Dock; Beggar Gang Martial Arts Transmission Conservative Elder.

lanchuan-p20.name: Pu Xiaoqi
lanchuan-p20.brief: The most popular young beggar on the Lianghuai grand docks. Whenever a merchant stall is shorthanded or a poor family cannot put food on the table, he hoists his carrying pole and rushes to help.
lanchuan-p20.role: Caokou Market; Beggar Gang Three-Bag Disciple; porter leader.

lanchuan-p21.name: Yan Shier
lanchuan-p21.brief: A renowned spymaster and news broker of the realm. Tingyu Tower handles thousands of secret dispatches daily, yet Tower Master Yan Shier enforces an iron rule: Tingyu Tower never tells lies, but it never tells the whole truth either.
lanchuan-p21.role: Qinghe City; Master of Tingyu Tower; one of the "Seven Friends of Lanchuan".

lanchuan-p22.name: Qiao Buduan
lanchuan-p22.brief: A famed master storyteller throughout the Lianghuai region. His signature trick is striking the gavel at the most critical life-or-death juncture—announcing, "To know what happens next, listen to the next installment," driving a hall full of tea guests to thump their chests in frustration.
lanchuan-p22.role: Qinghe City; head storyteller on the ground floor teahouse of Tingyu Tower.

lanchuan-p23.name: Bai Henian
lanchuan-p23.brief: Leader of the Lichun Troupe, who has spent a lifetime singing the saga of the Yang Clan Generals. Onstage, his desolately righteous high pitch moves listeners to tears; offstage, dozens of his acrobats and martial performers possess solid, formidable hand-to-hand combat skills.
lanchuan-p23.role: Sangma Town; troupe master of the Lichun Troupe; renowned *laosheng* (elder male role) master.

lanchuan-p24.name: Jiang Qinghe
lanchuan-p24.brief: A praised living Bodhisattva throughout the Lianghuai area. She flattened the threshold of the pharmacy specifically to let pushcarts carry the wounded through; she charges nothing to the poor and often covers the cost of herbal decoctions herself.
lanchuan-p24.role: Sangma Town; resident physician at Qinghe Pharmacy; former head disciple of Huichun Hall.

lanchuan-p25.name: Xuan Ci
lanchuan-p25.brief: Grand master and leader of a generation at Shaolin Monastery. Boundless in Buddhist doctrine, his Great Weituo Pestle and Great Vajra Palm shake the martial forest, earning him the title "Tiger-Taming Arhat."
lanchuan-p25.role: Shaolin Monastery; Abbot; supreme leader of the Buddhist realm.

lanchuan-p26.name: Xuan Ji
lanchuan-p26.brief: Master of the Discipline Yard whose name strikes dread into the monastery's warrior monks. Strictly upright, unforgiving, and unable to tolerate a single speck of dust; handles punishment for monks and lay disciples who break monastic precepts.
lanchuan-p26.role: Shaolin Monastery; Head of the Discipline Yard.

lanchuan-p27.name: Xuzhu
lanchuan-p27.brief: The lowliest, most timid novice at Shaolin's mountain gates. Bows with palms clasped to anyone he meets, speaks hesitantly, and his greatest daily wish is not misreading scriptures during morning and evening chants, and not spilling vegetarian noodle soup on pilgrims.
lanchuan-p27.role: Shaolin Monastery; young monk of the Guest Reception Quarters.

lanchuan-p28.name: Dingyan
lanchuan-p28.brief: A mysterious old monk who has swept fallen leaves in the silent Pagoda Forest behind Shaolin for forty years. Daily, he holds only a broom, circling the most ancient desolate pagoda.
lanchuan-p28.role: Shaolin Monastery; elder guardian monk of the Pagoda Forest.

lanchuan-p29.name: Fei Bin
lanchuan-p29.brief: The most powerful enforcer in the Songshan Sect second only to Zuo Lengchan. His "Great Songyang Divine Palm" possesses mountain-moving force; under the Five Sacred Mountains Command Flag, he oversees inspections at the foot of the mountain.
lanchuan-p29.role: Songshan Sect; Second Taibao, known as "Great Songyang Hand".

lanchuan-p30.name: Ji Wenmo
lanchuan-p30.brief: Proprietress of the copying workshop situated below the Shaolin gate for years. Beyond transcribing scriptures for customers, she pens dozens of anonymous damaged sutra fragments daily, labeled "Free Karmic Gift" for impoverished travelers.
lanchuan-p30.role: Temple Front Street; female proprietress of the Scripture Copying Workshop.

lanchuan-p31.name: Chang Shoutian
lanchuan-p31.brief: The leading farmer of Maihuang Village, who has tended Shaolin's monastery fields for fifty years. Both respectful and resentful toward the monks above, his greatest dread is the monastery's new accounting monks jacking up the land rent.
lanchuan-p31.role: Maihuang Village; Village Head and Shaolin tenant farmer.
lanchuan-p31.initial_place_label: Wheat Yellow Village and Thread of Sky

lanchuan-p32.name: Chang Xiaoqiu
lanchuan-p32.brief: The only literate girl in the village. Households ask her to calculate grain-borrowing deeds and field yield distributions. Fierce and unyielding, she dares to argue fiercely with Shaolin warrior monks over half a sack of wheat.
lanchuan-p32.initial_place_label: Wheat Yellow Village and Thread of Sky

lanchuan-p33.name: Song Yuanqiao
lanchuan-p33.brief: Eldest disciple of Grandmaster Zhang Sanfeng, managing all Wudang affairs on his master's behalf. His internal Pure Yang Boundless Skill is peerless. Broad-minded, humble, and gentle, he enjoys deep respect from both the righteous and underworld factions across the land.
lanchuan-p33.role: Mount Taihe; Head Administrator of Zixiao Temple; leader of the Seven Heroes of Wudang.

lanchuan-p34.name: Yu Lianzhou
lanchuan-p34.brief: The most skilled in martial arts and deepest in temperament among the Seven Heroes of Wudang. Creator of lethal techniques like the "Tiger Claw Extinction Hand." Though icy on the surface, he is fiercely protective of his sect and fellows.
lanchuan-p34.role: Mount Taihe; Executive Deacon of Zixiao Temple; Second Hero of Wudang.

lanchuan-p35.name: Song Qingshu
lanchuan-p35.brief: Only son of Song Yuanqiao and foremost among Wudang's third generation. Astonishingly gifted, he has mastered the essence of the Taiji Swordplay. Admired by youths of all sects wherever he goes, he carries the faint dignity of a future sect leader.
lanchuan-p35.role: Mount Taihe; head third-generation disciple of Zixiao Temple.

lanchuan-p36.name: Shen Guhe
lanchuan-p36.brief: A sword-obsessed Wudang disciple who stormed out of the sect ten years ago. Every day, he sits alone in the cliffside pavilion along the Hundred Steps Staircase drinking coarse tea, gazing toward the Golden Peak of Zixiao, all to demand an answer and justice from his former sect.
lanchuan-p36.role: Hundred Steps Staircase · Lone Pine Pavilion; exiled Wudang disciple.
lanchuan-p36.initial_place_label: Hundred-Step Stairs and Lonely Pine Pavilion

lanchuan-p37.name: Yun Shu
lanchuan-p37.brief: A Daoist nun at Zixiao Temple responsible for attending to the daily needs of registered disciples and external guests. Extremely placid and kind-hearted, whenever she encounters an impetuous junior, she always first serves a cup of Cloud-and-Mist Tea to clear the mind and cool inner fires.
lanchuan-p37.role: Mount Taihe · Daoist nun of Zixiao Temple.

lanchuan-p38.name: Qu A'qiao
lanchuan-p38.brief: The sharpest and most capable tea-picking girl on Cloud-and-Mist Tea Slope, raised alongside the ancient tea trees since childhood. This year, the "Mother Tree" halfway up the mountain suffered withered branches and scorched leaves. She has been rushing around seeking remedies, convinced that this is no curse of Heaven, but someone secretly poisoning its roots.
lanchuan-p38.role: Cloud-and-Mist Tea Slope · Tea-picking peasant girl.

lanchuan-p39.name: Qi Wujiu
lanchuan-p39.brief: An old wood-hauler hidden beneath the precipitous cliffs behind Zixiao Temple. Claiming to know no martial arts, he can nonetheless haul two hundred pounds of damp pine firewood over thousand-foot cliffs in a single breath as though treading on flat ground.
lanchuan-p39.role: Mind-Cleansing Ravine, back mountain of Mount Taihe · Reclusive old woodcutter; styling himself "Old Woodcutter Tao".

lanchuan-p40.name: Yue Buqun
lanchuan-p40.brief: Renowned across the world as the Leader of Mount Hua and the pillar of rectitude within the Five Mountains Alliance. His Violet Sunset Divine Skill is consummate, and he speaks constantly of benevolence, righteousness, and honor, earning deep veneration from scholars and commoners throughout Guanzhong.
lanchuan-p40.role: Jade Maiden Peak of Mount Hua · Sect Leader of the Mount Hua Sect; senior veteran of the Five Sacred Mountain Sword Sects, the "Gentleman Sword".
lanchuan-p40.initial_place_label: Jade Maiden Peak of Mount Hua

lanchuan-p41.name: Linghu Chong
lanchuan-p41.brief: The Eldest Disciple of Mount Hua Sect. Innately innocent and romantic, deeply addicted to wine, valuing loyalty above all, and endowed with breathtaking comprehension in swordsmanship. Recently, because he associated with Tian Boguang, an outcast of the demonic sect, he was ordered by his master Yue Buqun to face the wall on the secluded summit of Cliff of Contemplation for one full year.
lanchuan-p41.role: Senior Disciple of Mount Hua Sect; serving punishment in self-reflection on Cliff of Contemplation.
lanchuan-p41.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p42.name: Lu Dayou
lanchuan-p42.brief: The liveliest and most mischievous junior brother in Mount Hua Sect. Utterly devoted to Senior Brother Linghu Chong, he risks being punished by their master every day to smuggle fine wine and roast duck up the thousand-foot Cliff of Contemplation to bring him meals.
lanchuan-p42.role: Sixth Disciple of Mount Hua Sect; nicknamed "Six Monkeys".
lanchuan-p42.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p43.name: Lao Denuo
lanchuan-p43.brief: Second disciple of Mount Hua, barely younger than Yue Buqun himself. Diligent and meticulous in conduct, he manages all the burdensome chores of the sect, working tirelessly and earning the deep trust of his peers.
lanchuan-p43.role: Second Disciple of Mount Hua Sect; deep-cover mole for the Mount Song Sect.
lanchuan-p43.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p44.name: Zhou Zhiruo
lanchuan-p44.brief: The most cherished and gifted inner disciple of Master Miejue. Gentle as water on the outside, modest and courteous toward others, her swordplay radiates sharp spirit and brilliance. Having accompanied her peers down the mountain to Cangwu Ridge to procure spiritual herbs, every movement she makes draws admiration.
lanchuan-p44.role: Prime Disciple of the Emei Sect Leader.
lanchuan-p44.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p45.name: Ding Minjun
lanchuan-p45.brief: Renowned within the Emei Sect as a "poisonous porcupine". Relying on her seniority to bully and domineer over her peers, she stops at nothing to slander and suppress any martial sister whose beauty or talent surpasses her own.
lanchuan-p45.role: Senior Disciple of the Emei Sect's Fourth Generation.
lanchuan-p45.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p46.name: Du Ruo
lanchuan-p46.brief: Universally acknowledged as the foremost medical master along the great river. She established the ironclad rule of "Extinguishing Blades upon Entry": whether princes, generals, or notorious bandits, once inside Spring-Return Valley, all swords are sealed in chests; only life and death are weighed, not right and wrong.
lanchuan-p46.role: Cangwu Ridge · Hall Master of Spring-Return Hall; legendary Miracle Healer; one of the "Seven Friends of Lanchuan".

lanchuan-p47.name: Mo Wensheng
lanchuan-p47.brief: A recluse and madman dwelling deep in the poisonous miasma-filled abyss. Consummate in both medicine and poison, he behaves in total defiance of convention, believing that "without understanding poison, how can one fathom medicine?" He constantly tests potent, ruthless toxins on living, critically ill patients.
lanchuan-p47.role: Mist-Locked Gully · Eccentric Master of Poison; former Senior Disciple of Spring-Return Hall.

lanchuan-p48.name: Abbess Dingxian
lanchuan-p48.brief: A revered Buddhist nun leader among the Five Sacred Mountain Sword Sects. Though devoid of ambition for worldly supremacy, she possesses unshakeable inner composure. Facing Zuo Lengchan's threats of annexation, she consistently conquers strength with softness, standing firm and unyielding.
lanchuan-p48.role: Northern Peak Mount Heng Sect Leader; Abbess of White Cloud Nunnery.
lanchuan-p48.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p49.name: Yilin
lanchuan-p49.brief: The most beloved and innocent young nun across all of Mount Heng. Pure of heart without a speck of dust, she speaks softly and timidly. Distributing medicine and porridge to wounded soldiers and refugees at the gates of Falling Goose Pass, she earns the respect of all.
lanchuan-p49.role: Mount Heng Sect's White Cloud Nunnery · Youngest martial sister.
lanchuan-p49.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p50.name: Li Changfeng
