lanchuan-p50.brief: A Greenwood outlaw guarding the vital throat of Black Stone Station leading beyond the pass. His Cloud-Ripping Spear commands terror throughout the northern frontier. He upholds the rule of "Three cents of toll, never take a life"; those who refuse to pay must survive three thrusts of his spear.
lanchuan-p50.role: Outside Black Stone Station · Overlord of Stony Ridge; formerly one of the "Seven Friends of Lanchuan".
lanchuan-p50.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p51.name: Zhong Xia
lanchuan-p51.brief: The female manager stationed at the grand desert pass. Exceptionally adept at balancing interests, she thoroughly understands the appetites of roving desert bandits and garrison officers alike; her escort carts pass through the checkpoints without the slightest hesitation.
lanchuan-p51.role: Falling Goose Pass · Chief Manager of Wild Goose Escort Bureau Branch.

lanchuan-p52.name: Old Master Qin
lanchuan-p52.brief: The respected elder leading the desert oasis of Sandspring Village. Water-sharing rights from an ancient stone trough depend entirely on his word; passing merchant caravans wishing to draw water and replenish supplies must first place a copper coin before his table.
lanchuan-p52.role: Sandspring Village · Old Canal Master; former inner elder of the Kongtong Sect.
lanchuan-p52.initial_place_label: Sand Spring Village and Kongtong Terrace

lanchuan-p53.name: Chai Feng
lanchuan-p53.brief: A retired veteran escort chief living alone in an abandoned dynasty beacon tower for over a decade. Exactly where the quicksand lies and which spring contains alkali in the great desert are all etched into his memory; back in his prime, he personally guided countless escort apprentices along the northern route.
lanchuan-p53.role: Broken Beacon Tower · Reclusive veteran escort; frontier beacon tower keeper.
lanchuan-p53.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p54.name: Zhang Wuji
lanchuan-p54.brief: The youthful cult leader who commands millions of Ming Cult rebel troops and the worldly sect's sacred altars. Mastering both the Nine Yang Divine Skill and the Heaven and Earth Great Shift, his martial arts shake the ages, yet his conduct is marked by leniency and loving-kindness. He strives with all his heart to extinguish the century-old vendetta between the Ming Cult and the Six Great Sects.
lanchuan-p54.role: Bright Peak, far west of Frost Ridge; Thirty-Fourth Cult Leader of the Ming Cult.

lanchuan-p55.name: Zhao Min
lanchuan-p55.brief: A Mongol princess of peerless wit and strategy who has cast aside royal wealth and noble rank to roam the jianghu with Zhang Wuji. She commands a vast network of northern scouts and undercover agents who have moved south; with a simple wave of her hand, she can manipulate the overall chess match across Shaolin and the Five Sacred Mountains.
lanchuan-p55.role: At the side of the Ming Cult Leader; Princess Shaomin, daughter of Temür, Grand Marshal of the Armies of the Realm under the Mongol Yuan Dynasty.
lanchuan-p55.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p56.name: He Taichong
lanchuan-p56.brief: A grandmaster of the Orthic Dual-Polarity Swordplay who holds sole dominance over the western snowy mountains. His sword maneuvers are marvelous, treacherous, and deadly. Yet beneath his dashing and romantic veneer, he is cold-hearted, ungrateful, desperately henpecked, and obsessed with the Kunlun Sect's factional interests.
lanchuan-p56.role: Sect Leader of the Kunlun Sect; known as the "Iron Zither Gentleman".
lanchuan-p56.initial_place_label: Location described in the character’s profile

lanchuan-p57.name: Yan Hanlu
lanchuan-p57.brief: A world-renowned master of divine weapons, responsible for forging half of the swords worn by the sect leaders across the realm. Explosive, eccentric, and solitary, he upholds an ironclad rule: "Not an inch of raw iron shall be granted to those unworthy of holding a blade, even for ten thousand taels of gold."
lanchuan-p57.role: Master of Red Hearth Manor; the foremost master forgemaster in the Northern Marches.

lanchuan-p58.name: Yan Ji
lanchuan-p58.brief: The next pillar of Red Hearth Manor. Having thoroughly inherited her grandfather's mastery of smelting iron and reading steel, she is generous, open-hearted, and outspoken. She longs to market the manor's high-grade farming tools and refined-steel arrowheads across the northern tribes, bringing better livelihoods to the craftsmen of this bitter-cold frontier.
lanchuan-p58.role: Red Hearth Manor; female sword-forging instructor; direct granddaughter of Yan Hanlu.

lanchuan-p59.name: Lei Baishan
lanchuan-p59.brief: The acclaimed leader of thousands of hunters scattered across the Frost Ridge snow plains. Eking out a living amid deep mountains and bitter blizzards year-round, he established ironclad mountain ordinances: no hunting parties in spring, no taking pregnant beasts in winter; any mountain-crossing merchant caravan that heeds orders is guaranteed to cross the snowline in one piece.
lanchuan-p59.role: Cold Pine Fort; Chief Leader of the Cold Mountain Hunting Guild.

lanchuan-p60.name: Liu Chenzhou
lanchuan-p60.brief: A mysterious scholar dwelling alone in the windswept snowy crags of the extreme north. He never mentions his past or meddles in jianghu affairs, yet his every motion exudes the commanding aura of a grandmaster. His three timber cabins are wiped immaculate, without a single speck of dust.
lanchuan-p60.role: Listening Snow Hut; recluse of peerless martial arts; styles himself "Master Liu"; Eldest of the "Seven Friends of Lanchuan".

lanchuan-c03.name: Ferry Passenger
lanchuan-c03.description: A traveler shaped by river trade and salt winds. Hardy, observant, and equipped with a sealed letter and worn gear, stepping ashore into Lanchuan.
lanchuan-c03.profile: Having spent years laboring aboard coastal cargo barges, you know the tides, the feel of the oars, and how to stay watchful around cutpurses. With your old vessel seized upon the captain's demise, you stepped ashore with simple belongings and a sealed missive left in your care. Whether you honor that unverified errand or carve out an entirely new livelihood remains yours to decide.
lanchuan-c03.origin: A battered timber shack beside Chaoxin Ferry, where river currents meet the coastal tide. Wooden boats creak against morning pilings.
lanchuan-c03.opening_text: The morning tide recedes, leaving salty dampness on the old mooring ropes. By the shack door, Old Lu mends his hemp nets, nudging a low wooden stool toward you. Lan A'li strolls down the embankment carrying a basket of silver bream, inquiring if any boat is heading toward Yankou City today. The sealed letter rests quiet and heavy against your ribs. The muddy lane leads inland toward the bazaars, while the ferry creaks against the slipway, awaiting your first step.

lanchuan-c02.name: Escort Vanguard
lanchuan-c02.description: A pragmatic escort hire forged on caravan trails. Experienced with pack draft animals and basic saber forms, ready to carve a name in the trade.
lanchuan-c02.profile: Trained within the rank and file of the Yanxing Escort Agency at Qingping Lake, you know the weight of road dust and the cadence of trail warnings. Your saber handling was honed through long hauls across rough passes rather than refined courtyards. While the agency offers steady grain and reliable company, the sprawling trade routes beyond the gate offer ample room for your own ambitions.
lanchuan-c02.origin: The back courtyard of the Yanxing Escort Guildhall in Hedu Town. Packed dirt rings the weapons rack beneath high stone walls.
lanchuan-c02.opening_text: Morning frost still clings to the courtyard stone locks, where wooden practice blades rest in a rack. Little Yan brings over a steaming bowl of rice and pickled greens just as the iron chime rings thrice from the main ledger hall. Master Huo sets an escort token for Qinghe City upon the center table, scanning the yard to see who steps forward for the run. With hot food in hand and your saber within reach, you might step up to inspect the contract, or tend to your own errands first.

lanchuan-c01.name: Taoist Initiate
lanchuan-c01.description: A philosophical seeker educated at a mountain sanctuary. Skilled in breath cultivation and balanced forms, stepping into the mortal world to wander.
lanchuan-c01.profile: Having spent seasons as an initiate beneath the eaves of Mount Taihe, you have internalized basic breath-regulation and poised unarmed routines. Tradition dictates that true understanding requires tasting worldly joys and trials before settling upon a lifelong path. Carrying your traveling knapsack and copper pieces down the stone stairs, you are free to seek martial heights, scholarly insight, or secular wealth.
lanchuan-c01.origin: Outside the teahouse at Yingxian Town, nestled at the foot of Mount Taihe. Copper kettles steam beneath old pine rafters.
lanchuan-c01.opening_text: Sunlight filters through drifting mist onto the worn stone archway of Yingxian Town. Master Tu slides down his cedar shop shutters, placing a bowl of hot mountain brew on the damp table before you. Up the slope, the three thousand steps toward Lone Pine Pavilion glisten with dew, while pack-laden merchants and herbalists filter into the awakening streets. The teahouse keeper smiles and reminds you that the road is long; drink your fill before choosing which path to take.

lanchuan-heir.name: Martial House Heir
lanchuan-heir.description: Heir to an established martial household, personally trained since childhood and capable in your own right. You own 3,000 silver, a fine sword and protective gear. Begin at your family residence in Lankou City with an established name.

lanchuan-returning-escort.name: Returning escort
lanchuan-returning-escort.description: An experienced escort who knows the river and land routes. The old injury has healed, and there are six hundred and fifty taels in the chest. A boatman who owes you a favor is at the door.

lanchuan-weapon-blade.name: Short Saber
lanchuan-weapon-blade.description: A direct, committed cutting strike. The matching implement starts equipped; other forms remain learnable.

lanchuan-weapon-sword.name: Long Sword
lanchuan-weapon-sword.description: A compact sword form adds a small, explicitly priced guard. The matching implement starts equipped; other forms remain learnable.

lanchuan-weapon-staff.name: Staff
lanchuan-weapon-staff.description: Use the staff tip for brief control at a higher energy cost, subject to recovery protection. The matching implement starts equipped; other forms remain learnable.

lanchuan-weapon-spear.name: Spear
lanchuan-weapon-spear.description: A stronger linear thrust requires unblocked movement. The matching implement starts equipped; other forms remain learnable.

lanchuan-weapon-fist.name: Unarmed
lanchuan-weapon-fist.description: Close strikes retain a small guard; the wraps are no legendary weapon. The matching implement starts equipped; other forms remain learnable.

lanchuan-method-restorative-breath.name: Restorative Breathing
lanchuan-method-restorative-breath.description: Measured breathing recovers a little energy and health instead of attacking. This is a game-authored foundation, not a famous school’s secret art.

lanchuan-method-iron-breath.name: Rooted Guard Breathing
lanchuan-method-iron-breath.description: A rooted stance absorbs pressure while forgoing an offensive technique. This is a game-authored foundation, not a famous school’s secret art.

lanchuan-method-driving-breath.name: Driving Breath
lanchuan-method-driving-breath.description: Drive a forceful blow at the price of 4% maximum health and one injury each time. This is a game-authored foundation, not a famous school’s secret art.

lanchuan-s01.description: The inward breath feels warm and substantial, like sheltering coals on a cold night.
lanchuan-s01.background: Its great reputation can begin with one slow breath. Those demanding a miracle may not sit through the first incense stick.

lanchuan-s02.description: Bone and sinew open little by little with breathing; a still sleeve conceals no idle muscle.
lanchuan-s02.background: Shaolin teaching favors correctness over imposing poses. Copies outside the gate often miss the breath that closes the form.

lanchuan-s03.description: Before the body shifts, the way it receives force changes within the breath.
lanchuan-s03.background: The secret teaching is difficult not merely for its meridian names, but for knowing when not to force another clever turn.

lanchuan-s04.description: The circulation is intricate enough that even a pause must be deliberate.
lanchuan-s04.background: Its title invites rivalry; its pages mostly demand solitary work. A serious reader may linger over one ordinary word.

lanchuan-s05.description: Breath rises in layers, substantial within without requiring outward display.
lanchuan-s05.background: Huashan pupils lower their voices at the name. A sect’s reputation weighs on the pages and on the daily work they require.

lanchuan-s06.description: The breath is long and unhurried, like water warming early in a mountain hut.
lanchuan-s06.background: Mount Taihe’s instruction begins with not hurrying a breath. An old adept’s cup may be chipped, yet nothing spills.

lanchuan-s07.description: The cupped palm looks loose while the inner paths draw tight; releasing the practice is the difficult part.
lanchuan-s07.background: Tavern tales relish taking another’s strength. They rarely linger over what borrowed currents leave inside the taker.

lanchuan-s08.description: Gentle warmth follows a steady breath, strength kept beneath its calm.
lanchuan-s08.background: Emei’s inherited portion is not the whole scripture. Teaching what is understood matters more than claiming completeness through a celebrated title.

lanchuan-s09.description: A palm sends the whole frame outward; bringing it back shows another kind of skill.
lanchuan-s09.background: The first twelve forms have living teachers. The last six carry conflicting accounts: some ask about power, others why an old master stopped.

lanchuan-s10.description: The circles do not hurry; feet and waist give the moving hands a root.
lanchuan-s10.background: Spectators copy the hands while teachers crouch to inspect the feet. Half a misplaced step matters more than an incomplete circle.

lanchuan-s11.description: Several kinds of force inhabit one fist; the feeling afterward is more complicated than satisfaction.
lanchuan-s11.background: Kongtong put its warning in the name. The seven injuries are not addressed only to the opponent.

lanchuan-s12.description: The fingers gather firmly while the shoulders and back settle before release.
lanchuan-s12.background: The Shaolin art is no threatening finger pose. Repeated plain movements teach where the force actually travels.

lanchuan-s13.description: The palm comes darkly, as if a thin cold draft followed the sleeve.
lanchuan-s13.background: Its name travels faster than its teaching. People fear not merely the cold but the lingering hurt survivors do not care to describe.

lanchuan-s14.description: The hands leave space without loosening the stance; a small turn exposes habitual stiffness.
lanchuan-s14.background: Students first complain that it lacks effort. A teacher may let them stand in the empty shape until the urge to struggle tires.

lanchuan-s15.description: Many palm shapes still depend on orderly shoulders and elbows, never haste.
lanchuan-s15.background: A missed count in the hall sends the lesson back to its beginning. That plain restart is more tangible than the thousand-handed name.

lanchuan-s16.description: The eye follows an unattended opening rather than the glint of a blade.
lanchuan-s16.background: Feng Qingyang values insight, not using freedom from forms to conceal ignorance. A hint still has to be understood.

lanchuan-s17.description: Five traditions have different tempers; each transition begins with understanding the ground of the present one.
lanchuan-s17.background: An alliance brought manuals together without making their schools identical. The same line pauses differently at different gates.

lanchuan-s18.description: The tip moves calmly while the wrist watches the smallest deviation within a circle.
lanchuan-s18.background: A Wudang teacher may offer a plain bamboo switch first, to see whether a pupil can stop chasing the prestige of an edge.

lanchuan-s19.description: The staff moves cleanly through lifts and checks, attending to where an opponent can step.
lanchuan-s19.background: The Beggar Sect keeps its own teaching boundaries. Hearing forms named or watching the leader does not put the whole art in a spectator’s sleeve.

lanchuan-s20.description: Unusual turns do not always follow the directions familiar to Central Plains styles.
lanchuan-s20.background: Words and movements on the six tablets must be read together. Admiring their foreign mystery can still leave the first turn backward.

lanchuan-s21.description: The sword presses at startling speed, making the price of that speed all the more important.
lanchuan-s21.background: Tales celebrate overnight fame. Those who meet the teaching face its costs themselves; envy cannot choose for them.

lanchuan-s22.description: When the staff settles, heels and back must receive its weight together.
lanchuan-s22.background: Carrying and racking the staff belong to temple practice too. A weight one cannot set down safely should not be hurried toward another person.

lanchuan-s23.description: Each cut crowds close behind the last, almost stepping on its hem.
lanchuan-s23.background: Those praising speed at a tavern may ignore the recovery lesson. A lively edge still needs a hand capable of stopping it.

lanchuan-s24.description: The heavy pestle asks its wielder to settle before it moves.
lanchuan-s24.background: Long weapons look much alike on a rack. A turn in narrow ground reveals exactly what practice has missed.

lanchuan-s25.description: Long and short blades ask the eye not to favor the more conspicuous hand.
lanchuan-s25.background: Their unequal lengths contain the cooperation. Missing one loses not just weight but the spaces the pair was meant to cover.

lanchuan-s26.description: The frame opens upward with the breath, but the next footing must still be found.
lanchuan-s26.background: Worn mountain steps tell a plainer story than leaps in legend. Fine lightness begins with not misreading the landing.

lanchuan-s27.description: Close, light steps use a momentary support with particular care.
lanchuan-s27.background: The reed-crossing legend travels widely; beginners often stand on solid stakes. A story is not a ferryboat.

lanchuan-s28.description: Cloth gathers with the body as the steps change direction within a fading breath.
lanchuan-s28.background: Everyone knows Wei Yixiao’s title. Wide sleeves do not teach his art; students first learn the limits of their own legs.

lanchuan-s29.description: A change of shape resembles remembering another road, without disorder underfoot.
lanchuan-s29.background: Its reputation for survival appeals to travelers. Good practice often shows in taking a retreat while one remains available.

lanchuan-s30.description: Hear wind through cloth and a pole entering water before separating the sound that does not belong.
lanchuan-s30.background: Ferry practice need not begin with a blindfold. Song Laolu may simply ask for quiet beside the tide until guessing stops.

lanchuan-s31.description: A fine needle asks for a finer hand, following the patient’s breath first.
lanchuan-s31.background: The hall teaches retrieval and careful storage before display. Choosing whom to needle and why requires more than confidence.

lanchuan-s32.description: Root cuts, leaf backs and dried smells must each be remembered.
lanchuan-s32.background: Plain wooden tags hang from old gatherers’ baskets. A plant once misidentified may deserve the longest memory.

lanchuan-s33.description: Read ears and hesitant hooves before speaking through the reins.
lanchuan-s33.background: Northern traders save praise for buyers and patience for horses. Hurried travelers often discover the difference at the saddle straps.

lanchuan-s34.description: Strength travels through pole and hull, with room left in the waist above moving water.
lanchuan-s34.background: Boatmen learn footing in live currents and fishers watch a return before the tide. The first lesson is often not to boast about swimming.

lanchuan-s35.description: A pause changes an ordinary greeting; the listener looks at your hands before replying.
lanchuan-s35.background: Docks, escorts and beggars have their own speech. Memorizing phrases does not make everyone behind a door accept a fellow traveler.

lanchuan-s36.description: Hammer strokes vary in weight; fine work hides in the pause to examine heat.
lanchuan-s36.background: Apprentices first clean used weapons. Making something and caring for something old are two sides of the same craft.

lanchuan-basic-breath.description: The chest rises slowly; settle one breath before counting another.
lanchuan-basic-breath.background: Unnamed instruction often passes on this modest steadiness. Absence from famous manuals does not prevent a daily honest practice.

lanchuan-basic-blade.description: The short blade works close, recovering first to cover an opening.
lanchuan-basic-blade.background: Road-learned movements are rarely elegant. Cart shafts and luggage leave little room for a flourish near a companion’s shoulder.

lanchuan-basic-fist.description: Plain fists keep the caution learned on a rocking deck.
lanchuan-basic-fist.background: Boatworkers explain a punch through the gunwale beside them: a hard fist is little use if its owner falls off the plank.

lanchuan-i01.description: A thick spine and narrow blade make clear this is no wall ornament.
lanchuan-i01.background: Escort stores recognize such blades by old grip marks. Departing hands sharpen them; returning hands account for new nicks.

lanchuan-i02.description: A plain blue-steel blade takes a cool line of light beneath a wiping cloth.
lanchuan-i02.background: Similar forms appear at schools and smiths. Many buyers seek a usable daily sword rather than instant fame.

lanchuan-i03.description: Straight-grained waxwood thickens toward the end and brightens where palms work it.
lanchuan-i03.background: Many weapon lessons begin with this wood. Its modest name may accompany as many hours of practice as a famous sword.

lanchuan-i04.description: Before a swing, the weight of the spine fixes attention beside the wielder’s hand.
lanchuan-i04.background: Breaktide’s name travels with Green Salt Shoals. A worker hearing it may think of today’s food as readily as swordsmanship.

lanchuan-i05.description: A clear edge and precise finish meet a finely worked scabbard lining.
lanchuan-i05.background: Red Furnace Manor’s reputation does not end at the forge. A maker’s name travels with the weapon after delivery.

lanchuan-i06.description: The short, clean blade draws the eye through work left unfinished.
lanchuan-i06.background: A gift that never arrives can leave a concern longer-lived than iron. Its custodian must choose whether to tell this one’s story.

lanchuan-i07.description: Visible bamboo joints lead to a dark, polished iron head, more worn than the grip.
lanchuan-i07.background: At a ferry, tool and weapon blur: it poles the boat, checks driftwood and guards people beside the plank.

lanchuan-i08.description: Horn along the limbs carries the smell of worked leather and oil before the string is drawn.
lanchuan-i08.background: Mountain hunters keep bows clear of damp corners. A loud hunting tale rests on quiet maintenance nobody watches.

lanchuan-i09.description: Compact enough for a sleeve, it stops being an ornament once drawn.
lanchuan-i09.background: Short-weapon carriers know where cloth catches. Easy concealment does not remove the need for care or judgment.

lanchuan-i10.description: The long, slender blade rests like a held line of reflected water.
lanchuan-i10.background: Lake people connect its name to a reclusive master. Knowing of a sword gives no claim to the owner’s rack.

lanchuan-i11.description: Thick-seamed cloth takes sweat well; rolled sleeves soften with washing.
lanchuan-i11.background: Docks and practice yards share the cut. A patch need not be handsome if it lets an arm move freely.

lanchuan-i12.description: Heavy oiled cloth smells of tung oil, water following its folds downward.
lanchuan-i12.background: River workers would rather own fewer clothes than discover a leak after departure. Drying it in sunshine prepares for the next rain.

lanchuan-i13.description: Worn leather holds repaired straps and pale friction marks inside.
lanchuan-i13.background: Escorts may keep an old pair after replacement. It recalls no heroics, only shafts, reins and repeated raised hands.

lanchuan-i14.description: Dense fur closes at the neck, fine edges showing red against the light.
lanchuan-i14.background: Northern inn bargains begin with a hand at the collar. Softness is visible at a counter; warmth is tested in a pass.

lanchuan-i15.description: The pale robe hangs long but its cuffs can be rolled for work.
lanchuan-i15.background: Tea shops recognize its color through visiting pupils. Cloth alone is not a guarantee for everyone who wears it.

lanchuan-i16.description: Close-woven rattan meets stout bindings around the rim.
lanchuan-i16.background: Waterfolk favor things easy to hold. The hands rebinding this shield may know a boat’s knots just as well.

lanchuan-i17.description: The small copper plate is smooth against the body, with forming marks outside.
lanchuan-i17.background: Frontier makers need not polish its face to brilliance. Under clothing, an unchafing fit comes first.

lanchuan-rusty-blade.description: Rust yields to a narrow bright strip beside the nicked edge.
lanchuan-rusty-blade.background: A blade like this seldom has an impressive case label. A repairer asks what can be saved; its carrier chooses how far to take it.

lanchuan-foundation-1.description: A steady defensive foundation, practiced until protection follows the movement rather than arriving after the blow.
lanchuan-foundation-1.background: Published training notes carry the method. Copying its steps is only a beginning; proficiency comes from repeated, deliberate practice.

lanchuan-advanced-strike-1.description: Concentrates the practiced foundation into a direct strike, with a noticeable cost in energy.
lanchuan-advanced-strike-1.background: Published training notes carry the method. Copying its steps is only a beginning; proficiency comes from repeated, deliberate practice.

lanchuan-advanced-manual-1.description: Diagrams and correction marks fill the notes. Buying a copy does not replace the time spent studying it.
lanchuan-advanced-manual-1.background: An openly sold continuation for readers with the necessary foundation. Some keep it on a shelf until they are ready.

lanchuan-advanced-weapon-1.description: Fine lines meet along the edge, while the grip stays deliberately plain. Its balance rewards a practiced hand.
lanchuan-advanced-weapon-1.background: Inspection marks remain beside the fittings. A later owner can tune it further, but must work with the actual piece.

lanchuan-advanced-armor-1.description: Offset layers sit close during movement and distribute the force of a direct hit.
lanchuan-advanced-armor-1.background: The garment cannot read an opponent for its wearer. Careful users watch its wear and know when to step back.

lanchuan-foundation-recovery-1.description: Draws scattered energy back toward damaged tissue. Recovery is steady, but still draws on the user’s reserves.
lanchuan-foundation-recovery-1.background: Published training notes carry the method. Copying its steps is only a beginning; proficiency comes from repeated, deliberate practice.

lanchuan-advanced-balance-1.description: Leaves a defensive return flow within the strike, trading some impact for protection against the reply.
lanchuan-advanced-balance-1.background: Published training notes carry the method. Copying its steps is only a beginning; proficiency comes from repeated, deliberate practice.

lanchuan-make-advanced-weapon-1.background: Experienced makers add their own adjustments in the margins, while keeping track of real material and labor.
